"Емірати й саудівці роблять це щороку. Мільярд або два для них нічого не означають, і якщо це допомагає отримати бажаний результат, то це добре витрачені гроші".
У чому звинувачують Кушнера?
Наприкінці опублікованого уривка Меттью Коул підсумовує претензії, які можуть виникнути після цієї історії до Джареда Кушнера:
- Кушнер як старший радник президента офіційно був державним службовцем. Його посада вимагала не лише розкриття фінансової інформації відповідно до етичних норм, а й щорічного подання публічної та конфіденційної фінансової звітності. Оскільки він мав доступ до секретної державної інформації, Кушнер був зобов'язаний розкривати інформацію про будь-які банківські рахунки, де він був бенефіціаром або мав право підпису.
- Кушнер був зобов'язаний відповідно до федеральних урядових правил і вимог податкової служби розкрити свій доступ до рахунку. Якщо доступ Кушнера до рахунку в банку ОАЕ не був розкритий і схвалений урядом США та не був відображений у його податковій декларації, це є порушенням законодавства США.
- Фактично Мохаммед бін Заїд і Мохаммед бін Салман платили Кушнеру за вплив в уряді США. Будь-які спроби Кушнера вплинути на політику США в інтересах іноземного уряду, який надав йому гроші, робили б його агентом іноземної держави. Закон США вимагає від громадян, які лобіюють інтереси іноземної держави, повідомляти Міністерство юстиції про себе та країну, від імені якої вони працюють, пише Коул.
Реакція Кушнера та його адвокатів
Невдовзі після публікації уривка з книжки у Vanity Fair Джаред Кушнер відреагував на звинувачення на свою адресу.
"Твердження автора є абсолютно божевільними - нічого подібного ніколи не відбувалося. Ми офіційно спростували кожне з них, однак автор не зміг надати жодного доказу на їх підтвердження. Не було представлено ані банківських виписок, ані записів про грошові перекази, ані номерів рахунків, ані дат транзакцій - словом, жодних перевірюваних даних, які могли б підтвердити ці неймовірні звинувачення", - написав Кушнер у соцмережі X.
"У той період я був однією з найбільш прискіпливо досліджуваних людей у світі: до мене була прикута увага ЗМІ, щодо мене проводилися численні розслідування в Конгресі, а також розслідування під керівництвом спеціального прокурора. Я добровільно співпрацював зі слідством, надавши свідчення загальною тривалістю понад 30 годин. Жодне з цих звинувачень тоді не спливало - просто тому, що описані події ніколи не мали місця. Це обурливі вигадки, які подаються як "журналістське розслідування". До журналістики це не має жодного стосунку. Це суміш фантазій, художнього вимислу та заангажованої пропаганди, створена людиною, яка або психічно нездорова, або діє зі злим умислом", - написав Кушнер.
Адвокати Кушнера також заперечують будь-які незаконні дії, до яких міг бути причетний їхній клієнт. Автор книжки звернувся по коментар до представника Кушнера, і той заявив, що Джаред Кушнер не вчиняв жодних незаконних дій під час роботи радником президента; не має жодного уявлення про згадані рахунки; дотримувався всіх вимог закону під час взаємодії з іноземними урядами.
Крім того, в одному з коментарів адвоката, наведених у книжці, зазначено, що Кушнер "не укладав жодних угод чи домовленостей з лідерами або посадовими особами іноземних держав, які не були б погоджені з президентом Сполучених Штатів і не відповідали б найкращим інтересам Сполучених Штатів".

title: Сибіга та новий глава МЗС Румунії обговорили захист цивільного судноплавства у Чорному морі після атаки РФ на судно
content_c:
Міністр закордонних справ України Андрій Сибіга провів першу телефонну розмову з новопризначеним міністром закордонних справ Румунії Даном Некулаєску, під час якої сторони обговорили зміцнення безпеки в Чорноморському регіоні та спільну протидію російським загрозам цивільному судноплавству, повідомило Міністерство закордонних справ України в п'ятницю ввечері у своєму Телеграм.
"Ми повинні бути єдиними та рішучими в захисті цивільного судноплавства, забезпеченні свободи судноплавства та посиленні тиску на Росію. Одеський трикутник стане важливим форматом для подальшої роботи в цьому напрямі", – сказав Сибіга.
Глава українського МЗС наголосив, що нещодавня російська дронова атака на цивільне вантажне судно поблизу румунського узбережжя, внаслідок якої загинув громадянин України і ще троє українських членів екіпажу зникли безвісти, свідчить про масштаби наслідків агресії РФ для всього регіону.
Крім того, Сибіга привітав румунського колегу з призначенням на посаду та подякував Бухаресту за всебічну допомогу, зокрема за підтримку вступу України до Європейського Союзу. Міністри також обговорили питання захисту прав української національної меншини в Румунії та румунської національної меншини в Україні і домовилися підтримувати тісний контакт для реалізації спільних пріоритетів.
Як повідомлялося, В Чорному морі, приблизно в 24 км від порту Констанца (Румунія) затонуло торгове судно під прапором Коморських островів, після ураження дроном.

title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
content_c:
Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
- Published
Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, officials have said.
At least 34 others were injured as gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday.
The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing. No-one has admitted carrying out the attack.
In a news conference, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators which he described as a "group of extremists".
Jordan's King Abdullah II said authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties".
Initial reports indicated seven people had been killed in the attack. A government spokesperson later said six people had died, before officials again revised the death toll to seven.
CCTV footage, verified by the BBC, appears to shows three gunmen making their way from a road toward the church.
Two of the attackers are seen making their way on to what appears to be a vehicle entrance to the church grounds, before retreating briefly and returning with a third man. All three appear to be armed with handguns.
Separate footage believed to be from the aftermath of the attack appears to show several dead and wounded bodies on the ground amid chaotic scenes.
Witnesses have described scenes of panic inside the church as people threw themselves under pews searching for cover, moving away from the windows.
Prayers and screams could be heard throughout the building as some tried to flee.
Khalid al-Mdanat was at the church and told BBC Arabic the attack lasted around 15 minutes with "people trying to flee while the shooting was still active".
"People began pushing and throwing themselves to the ground," he said.
"Some were taking cover, some were cradling the dead, others were holding their sons close, some were grabbing their children and fleeing, while others were holding onto their friends who were with them at the church."
He said the gunmen left through the church doors and fled in a pickup truck "firing as they went".
Another witness said: "I heard something as if a war had just started.
"I thought it was an electrical short circuit. I looked, people lying on the ground, wounded. The scene was catastrophic."
A woman in the church said explosions rang out seconds after a prayer.
"The sound of machine guns started, and the sound of glass. We began to realise that something was happening.
"People started screaming.
The witness described how the situation "continued to escalate for 10 continuous minutes". Once she ran out the church she said "bodies were all in the courtyards".
Al-Faraya has described the incident as "painful and horrific" and "unparalleled in the history of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan".
There was a heavy security presence at the entrance to a hospital treating people injured in the incident in Karak, amid an atmosphere charged with anger among residents of the governorate, particularly the families of those injured and killed.
Many looked distressed as roads were closed around the facility and people were forced to park their cars and continue on foot.
Security measures were also tightened ahead of the visit by King Abdullah II to check on the injured.
The atmosphere around the hospital remained tense as the sound of crying and shouting was heard as families mourned their loved ones.
Many people appear shocked, frightened and angry. Some expressed frustration at what they described as "a failure to take a tougher approach towards terrorists".
Karak has a sizeable Christian community in the majority-Muslim Jordan.
Such violence is rare in the country, but deadly attacks have been carried out in the past.
Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun, a Christian head of state, said the "heinous terrorist attack" on the church "violated the sanctity of death and funeral mourners, contradicts all religious and humanitarian values," according to Lebanese media.
Additional reporting by Majdi Gousous, BBC Arabic.
description: Thirty-four people are also injured in the attack in southern Karak governorate, and a manhunt is now under way.

title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme
content_c:
Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme
- Published
Households will need to earn less than £110,000 to qualify for the government's new loan scheme for first-time buyers, or £140,000 for homes bought in London.
As first reported by The Times, external, the earnings limits are expected to be confirmed at the Budget next week.
The Your First Home scheme will offer government-backed equity loans worth 20% of new-build properties in England bought from participating developers.
The loans, which will also be subject to an initial interest-free period, are designed to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.
Previous schemes to help first-time buyers did not restrict eligibility by income but faced criticism for stoking house prices by allowing relatively wealthy households to borrow more.
Unveiling the Your First Home Scheme at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".
The Times reported that ministers had initially decided to set the earnings limits at £90,000 for homes outside outside London and £110,000 in the capital, before concluding this would deny access to too many middle-earning couples, such as teachers and nurses.
The government has also argued that the scheme will help to boost housebuilding, after ministers conceded they are set to miss a target to build 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.
Help to Buy
Labour has said the scheme will be funded by within existing government budgets, but is yet to provide details of which other areas will see their spending cut.
Developers taking part in the scheme will also be asked to contribute towards running costs.
The Home Builders Federation, which represents developers, has welcomed the plans and urged the government to move quickly to set up the scheme.
The Conservatives have however branded the proposals a "colossal admission of failure" of Labour's housebuilding record, and expressed concerns that the new developer levy could push up the price of new homes.
Like the Help to Buy scheme launched under the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government, the scheme will use equity loans, which are linked to changes in the value of properties they are used to purchase.
That scheme, which initially ran between 2013 and 2021, enabled all home purchasers to put down a 5% deposit on a newly built home worth up to £600,000.
Up to 20% of the cost of the home was funded by a shared equity loan, which was interest-free for the first five years.
A second version of that scheme, which ran from 2021 to 2023, restricted access to first-time buyers and applied regional-level price caps to the properties could be bought under the programme.

  - Published15 April

title: Before you crank up the thermostat, try these tips to keep your house warmer for longer
content_c:
Before you crank up the thermostat, try these tips to keep your house warmer for longer
- Published
As the UK braces for a chilly weekend, with powerful winds and heavy rain hitting parts of the country, people are looking for ways to bring some warmth to their homes without cranking up the heating just yet. It is autumn after all.
But with rising energy prices making heating homes more expensive, taking action now could pay off in the long run.
Experts warn, though, that if you're elderly or vulnerable you shouldn't compromise your health.
To help you prepare for the chillier months, BBC News asked families and experts to share their tips for keeping your home warm and cost-effective.
Eat hearty winter meals to warm you through
When it gets cold, many people turn to hot water bottles and blankets - but there are other ways to warm your body.
The British Heart Foundation recommends wearing lots of thin layers, rather than one thick layer, to trap the heat in.
Natalie, 29, says she's replaced some of the clothes she wears round the house with supermarket thermal leggings and tops and says "it's made such a difference".
Amber Waring, 27, from Devon, says she eats warm meals like stews and pasta bakes, and dances round the kitchen with her toddler while they cook to help keep warm.
Place a blanket under the bedsheet
With the clocks going back this weekend, the nights will be drawing in.
So if you have a thicker duvet, now is the time to bring it out. Some supermarkets sell winter duvets for under £20 - look for 10.5 tog or higher.
But there's something to be said for a craftily placed blanket, too. When it gets cold, Rebecca, 44, from Hertfordshire, sleeps with a blanket underneath her mattress, which she says stops draughts. "This was passed to me by my nan, she swore by it," she says. Others swear by placing a blanket above the mattress but under the bedsheet.
You can heat your bed before getting in with a hot water bottle, but make sure you check the expiry date. A guide by NHS Scotland, external says to let the water from the kettle cool for a few minutes before filling, only fill it two-thirds full, squeeze air out of the top before putting the stopper on, and don't hold it directly against your skin.
Using an electric blanket - to heat your bed before you get in or to wrap around yourself on the sofa - is "one of the cheapest ways" to stay warm, says Emily Seymour, energy editor at consumer organisation Which?. Testing by Which?, external shows it typically costs between 2p and 8p an hour to run an electric blanket at its highest setting. The London Fire Brigade, external says to unplug your blanket before you get into bed unless it has a thermostat control, not to use a hot water bottle at the same time, and replace it every 10 years.
Open curtains and let the sun in during the day
Keep doors closed to trap heat in the room you're in. You can place curtains or blankets over your doors for extra insulation.
Embrace the daylight. "If it's sunny outside, open the curtains so the sun heats the room, then shut them when the sun sets to keep the heat in," says Rebecca.
"If you're using a hot appliance, let the heat into the room," says Lianne Macfarlane, 40, from Cheshire. She recommends leaving your oven door open after using it to help warm your kitchen, though this isn't advised if you have small children who could injure themselves.
As well as curtains, other soft furnishings like rugs can help keep a room warm, says Seymour.
If you have a fireplace, lighting a fire to warm the room you're in can be cheaper than turning on the central heating for your whole house. Elin Davis, 30, from South Wales, says her log burner is more economical than turning her heating on - though she added that "logs can cost quite a bit these days".
Insulate your windows with bubble wrap
Gaps around doors can cause heat to escape, so place draught excluders around your door frames. You don't need to buy them - you can use towels or stuff socks into a pair of tights.

These include using foam strips, sealant and specialist chimney draught excluders if you don't use your fireplace. Things such as extractor fans and purpose-built ventilation shouldn't be blocked, she adds.
If your windows are single-glazed, then Sophie Burr of charity National Energy Action suggests looking at secondary glazing or investing in thermal curtains to help keep the heat in. Or for a cheaper option, some people suggest placing bubble wrap on your windows.
Even though it may be tempting, don't keep your windows closed all the time. Seymour notes that it's important to allow some ventilation in your house to prevent damp.
Use central heating wisely
"I wouldn't recommend not having your heating on at all," says Seymour, pointing to both the health issues this can cause as well as how pipes can freeze over.
But there are ways you can use heating wisely. These include checking whether your energy supplier offers cheaper prices at off-peak times, bleeding your radiators so that they're more efficient, and turning your heating up in small increments until you reach the right temperature. If you have furniture in front of your radiator, then try moving it to avoid blocking the heat.
You can also buy dedicated radiator foil or make your own with kitchen foil to reflect the heat back into the room rather than losing it through the walls, says Burr. She points out that about 35% of heat that comes from radiators is lost through walls.
Cora Harrison, 34, from Wakefield, says that she only turns the radiators on in the rooms her family is using and keeps the heating on at a low level when they're on holiday to avoid mould or pipes bursting. Some radiators have a snowflake symbol on the valve that activates the frost protection setting, meaning that if the room gets very cold, the radiator warms slightly to stop the pipes from bursting.
Another way to potentially reduce energy bills is to lower the flow temperature of your combi boiler. If you book a boiler service, an engineer can do this for you.
You can also find free warm spaces such as libraries and community centres in your area by looking online or contacting the council. Some spaces also provide free hot drinks.
Will energy bills rise further?
Household energy prices are set to soar in January, with a typical bill expected to jump by £276 a year, according to a forecast last month from consultancy Cornwall Insight. The 16% predicted increase would mark the biggest rise for four years.
Rising bills are "particularly concerning for people with kids, people with health conditions and the elderly," says Emily Jeremy, project manager at Manchester South Central Foodbank.
An estimated 9.4% of households in England lived in fuel poverty in 2025, according to the latest government figures, external.
Rodney Winchester, 65, from Thetford, who spoke to BBC News through the charity Christians Against Poverty, says he's "extremely worried" about rising energy prices. Because of health conditions, he says he has to keep the heating on throughout winter but is concerned he won't be able to afford it.
"It's so scary," Rodney says, adding that he's been cutting back on food spending and keeps getting ill in the cold weather.
If you are struggling with prices, the debt charity StepChange recommends checking whether you qualify for any additional support, like the Warm Home Discount and Winter Fuel Payment. It also advises contacting your energy supplier, which may be able to agree an affordable repayment plan or discuss support schemes.

title: Embattled Greens senator Jordon Steele-John confirms leave from parliament after allegations against him made public
content_c:
Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he will not attend parliament next week as the embattled Greens senator apologises for publicly releasing the letter outlining the claims against him.
On Saturday afternoon, Steele-John removed a social media post containing a three-page letter marked as “confidential” sent to the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, earlier this month. The letter urged an investigation into allegations he had acted inappropriately towards women between 2017 and 2025.
Steele-John has denied all allegations made against him.
The Western Australian senator said he’d heard the full letter had been circulating online and “didn’t want to be seen as hiding from it”.
“I’m now not sure that was the right call and I’ve taken it down. I am really sorry for any additional stress it caused,” he said on social media.
After days of confusion following historical complaints about alleged misconduct were publicly aired in the media, the now-deleted statement posted to social media late Friday night said he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be “unacceptable”.
He would instead focus on seeing through an independent investigation to its conclusion, he said.
“Over the past few days there has been a growing chorus calling on me not to attend parliament next week. I have explored attending digitally but have been informed that would also be unacceptable,” Steele-John said.
Steele-John said a precedent of keeping parliamentarians out of parliament after “allegations of allegations” were made had now been set.
“Had an allegation or complaint been made against me, I would have taken these actions immediately,” he said.
The 32-year-old senator’s attendance in parliament for the remainder of the year had been uncertain after a public stoush with Shoebridge over whether he was on leave during the investigation.
The complaints are now subject to an independent investigation commissioned by the WA Greens and have been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission.
Shoebridge claimed Steele-John had requested leave and he accepted it last week after seven party members penned a letter to the leader urging an investigation into the claims.
The three-page letter sent on 13 October, and first published by the Nine newspapers, said the authors had been “made aware of multiple allegations of serious misconduct” against Steele-John about his “behaviour in the presence of women”.
The letter referred to an allegation of sexual harassment at a Greens campaign event in 2024 that the alleged victim had not reported out of fear of backlash. The letter provided no further detail.
In another, the authors referred to an allegation of “serious sexual misconduct” in 2025. Steele-John later responded this was alleged by a former partner and was investigated by Western Australian police with a finding of “no charges”.
Guardian Australia has confirmed the WA police told Steele-John the investigation was closed in May with no charges.
Also contained in the letter was a reference to a disparaging nickname for Steele-John – “feels on wheels” – which the authors said implied he had a reputation for acting inappropriately.
“To be clear, all signatories to this letter know that an allegation does not equate to a fact and/or guilt. We simply believe that it is in the party’s best interests to ensure that every allegation is investigated thoroughly, in alignment with community and member expectations,” the letter’s authors wrote.
Steele-John was defiant in a lengthy statement last Sunday, rejecting the allegations against him, denying he agreed to take leave from parliament and accusing an internal faction within the Greens of playing “nasty political games” in their decision to release the letter to the media.
Steele-John said any claims of his alleged behaviour should be investigated “fairly and thoroughly” but accused an “unofficial faction” within the WA branch of releasing the complaint letter to the media in a bid to oust him from the Senate.

title: Briton facing forced separation from baby son after Sweden orders his deportation
content_c:
A British photographer is facing deportation from Sweden and forced separation from his 16-month-old son after authorities ruled in favour of the country’s immigration interests.
Simon Montgomery’s application to remain after the birth of his son last year was rejected on several grounds by Sweden’s migration agency, a decision that was then upheld by the migration court.
He is appealing to the higher migration court, arguing that he has EU freedom of movement rights as his son is a German citizen through his mother. “I am not here because I want to be in Sweden, I am only in Sweden to be with my son,” he said.
The couple separated shortly after the child was born but Montgomery, who grew up without his father in his life, said he was determined to stick around and be there for his newborn.
The pair have legally recognised joint custody, with a parenting agreement that meant his time with his son increased as he got older and no longer needed night-time breastfeeding.
He said he saw his son three days a week and took an active part in his care and daily routine with a “stable parenting plan” agreed via discussions with the municipal family law service.
He moved to Sweden after Brexit so was not entitled to any withdrawal agreement residency rights, but applied to stay on the basis he was the father of an EU citizen.
Montgomery said it was shocking that Sweden was prepared to separate a son from his father, even though the child had rights under EU law as well as international conventions. “Everything in Sweden is about the children’s right to both parents,” Montgomery said.
“But this seems to be ignoring all of that, when it comes around to immigration. Sometimes I feel like people don’t know what happens here. That’s why it’s so important to have these stories told.
“Everyone’s so friendly here; society works and things are nice. And when you tell them what’s happened, they just look shocked. They think you must have done something wrong, and when I explain I have done nothing wrong they just don’t understand.”
Montgomery said he was unable to leave Sweden to see elderly relatives in the UK for fear he would be blocked from returning to be with his son.
“It’s almost like torture in some ways, like having to make these decisions between staying to fulfil your parenting roles and not being able to visit my 98-year-old grandmother back in the UK and say my goodbyes,” he said.
His residency application, made when his son was six months old, was rejected last December by the migration agency on the grounds there was no evidence he had “actual care” for the child, who at that point still stayed overnight with his mother.
It also said he was free to maintain a relationship with his son from afar as he could enter the country visa-free and “still have the opportunity to visit the child in Sweden”.
He appealed against the decision but the court this month sided with the authorities, which assessed, according to the ruling, that the “state’s interest in regulated immigration outweighs your interest in the protection of your private and family life in a proportionality assessment”.
Montgomery said he was taken aback by the court’s suggestion he did not need to be in Sweden full-time because he could visit his son by entering the country as a visitor. “Because I can come here visa-free, [they say] it shouldn’t interrupt my parenting ability. That’s crazy because I look after my son three days a week now … and overnights are about to start very soon.”
According to court papers, the decision to reject an application for residency and a simultaneous decision that he should be deported was made “primarily on the grounds that he had not demonstrated that he met the conditions for the right of residence as a family member of an EEA citizen”.
His lawyer argued that if he were “forced to leave Sweden, this would undermine the process and create instability for his son”. They added: “His son is an infant and is in a critical attachment phase where it is in his best interest to have both parents physically present and actively involved.”
They argued that the boy’s father’s presence was “particularly important” because his former German partner did not have a family network to rely on if she was sick or at appointments.
“Deportation would constitute a disproportionate interference in their family life,” they said, arguing that the lower migration court had interpreted “actual care” – evidence of a child’s relationship with a parent – “too narrowly on the grounds that the son primarily lives with his mother”.
They alleged forcibly separating a son from his father would violate article 8 of the European convention of human rights.
Montgomery is appealing against the case to the higher court but said he wanted to share the story so people understood how immigration law was being implemented.
Sweden’s migration agency has been approached for comment. The German government said it could not comment on the case.

title: Trump eases Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
content_c:
Trump eases some Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
October 23, 2026
US President Donald Trump has lifted some of the tariffs imposed on Canada amid an economic row with the US' neighbor to the north, which peaked this summer.
The White House on Friday said the easing of tariffs will apply to products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment."
The changes will take effect on October 30.
While the latest move cuts some of the tariffs, it also imposes new levies on goods including carpets, certain valves and waste products, the White House said.
What do we know about the Canada tariffs relief?
The White House said the president was seeking to offset "the burden to US commerce while better serving the public interest.''
The move comes less than two weeks ahead of the November midterm elections, where Republican candidate Susan Collins is locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson in Maine.
Collins said on Friday she had addressed the tariffs with Trump's top trade negotiator, Jamieson Greer, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. The senator said she was acting out of concern for "the toll tariffs are taking on Maine families, businesses, farmers, and growers.''
"Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense," Collins said.
She added that she had asked for tariff relief and vowed to "encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbor, ally, and largest trading partner."
Why did Trump impose tariffs on Canada?
Washington and Ottawa have been locked in a trade dispute since Trump returned to the White House last year.
Trade tensions intensified when talks broke down in August, with Trump announcing a 50% levy on some Canadian goods and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing retaliatory tariffs.
On Friday, Trump told reporters that "Canada is working very hard to make a deal with us."
Edited by: Rana Taha

title: News: Friedrich Merz auf CSU-Parteitag, Wahl in Serbien, Anhänger feiern Le Pen, Stevie Wonder in Hannover
content_c:
Die Lage am Morgen Bitte recht freundlich – Merz muss zu Söder
- Merz muss zur Schwesterpartei – gemütlich wird's nicht
- Anhänger feiern Le Pen – in einem Land, das sich selbst bekämpft
- Ende eines Autokraten? – Serbien wählt
Wie wird Merz auf Söder antworten?
Der Kanzler ist heute zu Gast beim CSU-Parteitag. Da gehört es dazu, die gute Beziehung zwischen CDU und CSU zu betonen. Doch wenn sich Friedrich Merz die Rede von Markus Söder gestern angehört hat, werden ihm die vielen Spitzen nicht entgangen sein, die der CSU-Chef Richtung Berlin abfeuerte.
Söder wies darauf hin, dass die Umfragewerte der CSU in Bayern deutlich höher sind als die der Union im Bund. »Vielleicht sind wir tatsächlich der stärkste Teil der Union«, rief er. Steuererhöhungen, Schulden, Streit – all das passt ihm bei der Bundesregierung nicht. »Zusammenreißen, Arbeit machen und Erfolge haben« – darauf komme es jetzt an.
CSU-Chef Söder auf Parteitag: »Vielleicht sind wir tatsächlich der stärkste Teil der Union«
Foto: Wolfgang Maria Weber / IMAGO
Am interessantesten aber war Söders Botschaft zum Schluss. Er stellte sich demonstrativ hinter seine Parteifreundin Ilse Aigner als Bundespräsidentin. Kurz zuvor hieß es aus CDU-Kreisen, die CDU müsse den Anspruch haben, eine eigene Kandidatin, einen eigenen Kandidaten zu präsentieren. Der Applaus der Christsozialen für Söder war laut. »Macht das morgen noch mal bei Friedrich Merz«, empfahl er.
Meine Kollegin Maria Fiedler aus dem SPIEGEL-Hauptstadtbüro schätzt die Lage für den Kanzler so ein: »Wenn Merz klug ist, verzichtet er darauf, in seiner Rede länger auf Aigner einzugehen oder eine Konfrontation auf offener Bühne zu suchen.«
Wer sich nun aber hinter welche Kandidatin oder welchen Kandidaten für das höchste Staatsamt stellt, darauf sollten sich CDU und CSU bald einigen.
- Mehr Hintergründe: Gönnt die CDU der CSU eine Bundespräsidentin?
Das zerrissene Land
Proteste werden in Frankreich heute sowieso wieder erwartet. Und die Regierung von Präsident Emmanuel Macron hat schon angekündigt, dass sie hart einschreiten werde gegen jeden Exzess. Doch in Frankreich ballen sich in diesem Herbst die Konflikte.
»Ein halbes Jahr vor der Präsidentschaftswahl ist Frankreich gesellschaftlich und politisch zerrissen wie wohl noch nie seit der 68er-Revolution«, sagt mein Kollege Leo Klimm, Frankreich-Korrespondent des SPIEGEL.
Rechts-außen-Politikerin Le Pen: Ausgerechnet Orléans
Foto: Stephane De Sakutin / AFP
Denn zu den landesweiten Protesten kommt ein weiterer Konflikt hinzu: In der Provinzstadt Orléans treffen sich am Wochenende 10.000 Anhänger von Marine Le Pen, um die Rechtsaußen-Politikerin auf einem Parteitag zu feiern. Und es werden auch Zehntausende Gegendemonstranten erwartet.
Orléans ist die Stadt von Jeanne d'Arc, der französischen Nationalheldin, die 1429 mit ihren Truppen die Engländer aus der Gegend um Orléans vertrieben hat. Damals war es ein Kampf von innen nach außen, Franzosen gegen Engländer. Heute bekämpft Frankreich vor allem sich selbst.
- Mehr Hintergründe: Wie gefährlich ist die neue, staatstragende Marine Le Pen?
Geht in Serbien eine düstere Ära zuende?
Mal sehen, wie die Welt Anfang November aussehen wird. In der Zwischenzeit stehen wichtige Abstimmungen an: Die Stichwahlen für die Präsidentschaft sowie für wichtige Gouverneursämter in Brasilien an diesem Sonntag. Ebenfalls Sonntag finden Parlamentswahlen in Serbien statt. Bulgarien stimmt am selben Tag über die Präsidentschaft ab. Israel hat für den 27. Oktober die Wahl zur Knesset angesetzt. Und am 3. November 2026 kommen dann die US-Midterms.
Bleiben wir heute erst mal in Serbien, denn für Deutschland wird es geradezu täglich wichtiger, wie es um Europa steht. Die USA als Verbündete werden immer unzuverlässiger und Russland wird immer bedrohlicher.
Serbiens langjähriger Machthaber Vučić: Möchte Ämter tauschen
Foto: Oliver Bunic/ AFP
Serbien steckt jetzt schon lang im Beitrittsverfahren zur EU fest. Das Land hat sich schlechter entwickelt, als Brüssel zu Beginn des Verfahrens erwartet hatte. Auf dem Korruptionsindex von Transparency International ist Serbien 2025 auf den 116. Platz von 182 Ländern abgerutscht – in Europa war die Lage nur in Russland, Belarus und in der Türkei schlechter.
Verantwortlich dafür ist der langjährige Machthaber Aleksandar Vučić. Er war bis vor Kurzem Staatspräsident. Weil er als solcher nach zwei Amtszeiten nicht mehr kandidieren darf, zielt er jetzt auf einen Ämtertausch: Er würde bei einem Sieg seiner rechtspopulistischen Serbischen Fortschrittspartei (SNS) neuer Ministerpräsident werden.
Im Land formiert sich nun schon seit knapp zwei Jahren deutlicher Widerstand gegen Vučić und seine Partei. Mein Kollege Jörg Schindler war gerade in Serbien und hat einen Stimmungsbericht mitgebracht: Dem Regime, so schreibt er, sei diesmal ein Gegner erwachsen, der aus den Fehlern früherer Protestbewegungen gelernt habe.
- Die ganze Geschichte hier: Stürzt in Südosteuropa der nächste Langzeitautokrat?
Hier geht’s zum aktuellen Tagesquiz
Noch mehr Rätsel wie Viererkette, Wordle und Paarsuche finden Sie bei SPIEGEL Games.
Gewinner des Tages…
…ist der US-Musiker Stevie Wonder.
Deutschlandbesucher Wonder: Triumph des Menschlichen
Foto: epa Renee Hannans / dpa
Er gibt heute in Hannover sein erstes von zwei Deutschlandkonzerten zum 50-jährigen Jubiläum seines Albums »Songs For The Key of Life«. Wonder wird dabei alle darauf versammelten Lieder singen.
Ich habe gestern ins Album reingehört und alte Bekannte wiedergetroffen: den Song »Love’s in Need of Love Today« und »Isn’t She Lovely«. Dann habe ich an die künstliche Intelligenz gedacht und daran, dass sie eine Stimme wie die von Wonder von sich aus nie erfinden würde. Denn im eigentlichen Sinne schön klingt diese Stimme nicht. Dafür aber so freundlich, so eigen, so weit weg von virtuellen Imitationen, dass sie sich heute anhört wie ein Triumph des Menschlichen.
Die jüngsten Meldungen aus der Nacht
- Israel startet »Anti-Terror-Operation« im Westjordanland: Seit dem Abend geht Israels Armee eigenen Angaben zufolge gegen Terroristen im Westjordanland vor. Damit reagiere man auf den Angriff vom Morgen, heißt es. Am Dienstag wird in Israel gewählt.
- Bremens Bürgermeister warnt vor Extremismusklausel im Länderfinanzausgleich: Weniger Geld, weil AfD oder Linke ein Bundesland regieren? Andreas Bovenschulte kann den CSU-Vorschlag nicht nachvollziehen: »Das wäre reine Willkür.«
- Brand in einstigem Nazi-Berghaus am Obersalzberg: Errichtet wurde das Gebäude im damaligen »Führersperrgebiet« in Berchtesgaden. In der Nacht stand das Kehlsteinhaus auf 1834 Metern Höhe in Flammen. Nach ersten Erkenntnissen war niemand in dem heutigen Gasthof.
Heute bei SPIEGEL Extra: Mit diesen 23 Tipps wird Ihr Urlaub mit Freunden schön und nicht schrecklich
[M] Undine Meinke / DER SPIEGEL; Foto: Lubitz + Dorner / plainpicture
Sie wollen mit Freunden verreisen? Das kann grandios werden, aber auch ruckelig. Hier sind Fallstricke und Freuden von A bis Z – und eine Hilfe, wenn der Gruppenhonk nervt.
Ich wünsche Ihnen einen guten Start in den Tag.
Ihre Susanne Beyer, Autorin der Chefredaktion

title: CSU-Chef Söder spricht von "Herausforderung für die Demokratie"
content_c:
AfD, Linke und Lebenshaltungskosten Söder spricht von "Herausforderung für die Demokratie"
CSU-Chef Söder sieht die Demokratie vor großen Herausforderungen. Er forderte zudem finanzielle Entlastungen für die Bevölkerung. Es müsse etwas passieren, betonte der bayrische Ministerpräsident im Interview mit den tagesthemen.
Bundesweit stand die Union in Umfragen zuletzt schlecht da. Im DeutschlandTrend erreichte sie sogar historische Tiefstände. In Bayern liegt die CSU hingegen weiterhin vorn - wenn auch mit Abschlägen.
Auf das schwache Abschneiden der Union bei jungen Wählern angesprochen, verwies CSU-Chef Markus Söder auf eine Herausforderung für die Demokratie insgesamt. "Es wäre zu einfach, darauf zu rekurrieren, dass es für eine Partei schwierig ist", sagte Söder im Interview mit den tagesthemen.
Mit Blick auf die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt sprach er von "Extremisten", die Linken in Berlin nannte er "radikale Gruppen", denen wolle man etwas entgegensetzen. "Wir setzen dagegen ein klares Signal auf Offenheit, auf Hightech, auf Zukunft, keine Schulden gerade für die Jungen", so Söder.
Söder fordert Entlastungen
Zugleich kritisierte Söder die hohen Lebenshaltungskosten. Es gebe aus seiner Sicht nicht genügend Einsparungen in Bereichen, in denen bereits Veränderungen vorgenommen worden seien. Als Beispiel nannte er die Umstellung vom Bürgergeld auf die Grundsicherung. Auch die Kosten im Bereich Migration seien trotz des Rückgangs der illegalen Migration nicht gesunken, kritisierte der CSU-Chef. "Das kann nicht sein", betonte Söder. In diesen Bereichen brauche es erneut einen Kassensturz.
Außerdem brauche es ein Signal für Entlastung, etwa bei der Kalten Progression oder der Stromsteuer. "Es muss was passieren, denn ansonsten geht die große Mehrheit der Bevölkerung nicht mit." Angesichts der hohen Lebenshaltungskosten forderte Söder: "Wir müssen eine Koalition mit dem Volk machen. Wir müssen aufs Volk hören und nicht am Volk vorbeireden."
Plädoyer für Ilse Aigner
Mit Blick auf die im nächsten Jahr anstehende Wahl eines Nachfolgers oder einer Nachfolgerin von Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier sprach sich Söder erneut für seine CSU-Parteikollegin Ilse Aigner aus. Sie sei eine "sehr gute Kandidatin" für das höchste Staatsamt. "Eine Persönlichkeit mit Herz, mit Verstand und mit Erfahrung."
Söder sprach sich zugleich dafür aus, dass "die drei Parteivorsitzenden der Koalition - CDU, CSU und SPD - gemeinsam einen Vorschlag machen".

title: Erneute Wahlverschiebung in Guinea-Bissau: Politisches Chaos hält an
content_c:
Guinea-Bissau: Bleibt das Land im politischen Chaos gefangen?
23. Oktober 2026
Die für den 6. Dezember 2026 angekündigten Parlaments- und Präsidentschaftswahlen in Guinea-Bissau finden nicht wie geplant statt. Aly Silva, Sprecher des Übergangs-Premierministers Ilídio Vieira Té, bestätigte der DW, dass die Abstimmung bis auf Weiteres verschoben wird. Ein neuer Termin steht nicht fest. Zunächst wolle sich die Regierung im Kabinett beraten und anschließend öffentlich mitteilen, wann gewählt werden soll. Ob die Wahlen 2027 oder erst 2028 stattfinden, ist offen.
Die politische Krise geht auf den 26. November 2025 zurück. Drei Tage zuvor hatten die Menschen in Guinea-Bissau ein neues Parlament und einen Präsidenten gewählt. Noch bevor die offiziellen Ergebnisse bekannt gegeben wurden, übernahm das Militär die Macht und setzte den Wahlprozess außer Kraft. Sowohl der damalige Präsident Umaro Sissoco Embaló als auch sein Herausforderer Fernando Dias da Costa hatten den Wahlsieg für sich beansprucht.
Die Militärführung hat eine Rückkehr zur verfassungsmäßigen Ordnung versprochen. Doch die angekündigten Neuwahlen rücken erneut in die Ferne. Für den Juristen und politischen Analysten Cabi Sanhá kommt die Verschiebung nicht überraschend. Nach dem Putsch sei kaum etwas unternommen worden, um die Voraussetzungen für glaubwürdige Wahlen zu schaffen.
"Die Verschiebung war absehbar", sagt Sanhá im DW-Interview. Zwar sei der 6. Dezember als neuer Wahltermin festgelegt worden. "Aber es wurde nichts getan, damit diese Wahlen tatsächlich stattfinden können."
Fehlende politische Freiheiten
Die Übergangsregierung begründet die Verschiebung mit den fehlenden organisatorischen und politischen Voraussetzungen. Die Frist für die Einreichung der Kandidaturen lief bereits am 6. Oktober ab. Die Parteien und möglichen Kandidaten hatten ihre Bewerbungen nicht eingereicht. Nach Angaben des Premierministers hatten die Parteien zuvor auch keine Kongresse abgehalten, um ihre Kandidaten zu bestimmen.
Sanhá sieht darin nicht allein ein organisatorisches Problem. Er verweist auf die Einschränkungen politischer Aktivitäten und den fehlenden Dialog mit den zentralen Akteuren des Wahlprozesses. Parteien und Zivilgesellschaft seien nicht ausreichend einbezogen worden. Auch die Vermittlungsbemühungen der Westafrikanischen Wirtschaftsgemeinschaft ECOWAS und Senegals hätten bislang keine Lösung gebracht.
"Freie, transparente und inklusive Wahlen sind nur möglich, wenn man zuvor die Voraussetzungen dafür schafft", sagt der Jurist. Dass Parteien ihre Kandidaten nicht aufgestellt haben, betrachtet er deshalb auch als Folge der politischen Rahmenbedingungen. "Wie sollen Parteien Kandidaten aufstellen, wenn politische Aktivitäten im Land eingeschränkt sind? Sie können weder ihre Parteitage abhalten noch Versammlungen organisieren."
Führende Oppositionspolitiker halten sich zudem im Ausland auf. Domingos Simões Pereira, Vorsitzender der größten Oppositionspartei PAIGC, durfte im Juli 2026 aus der Haft nach Portugal reisen, um sich medizinisch behandeln zu lassen. Er war zuvor im Zusammenhang mit Ermittlungen zu einem mutmaßlichen Putschversuch in Untersuchungshaft genommen worden. Deine Verteidigung bestreitet die Vorwürfe und kritisiert das Verfahren als "politisch motiviert".
Die Abwesenheit wichtiger Oppositionsvertreter und die eingeschränkten Möglichkeiten politischer Organisation erschweren einen Wahlprozess, der eigentlich den Übergang zu einer zivilen Regierung ermöglichen sollte.
Ein Wahltermin ohne neuen Zeitplan
Wie es nun weitergeht, ist unklar. Nach Angaben des Regierungsmitarbeiters Aly Silva will sich die Übergangsregierung zunächst im Kabinett beraten. Erst anschließend soll ein neuer Wahltermin öffentlich bekannt gegeben werden. Einen konkreten Zeitplan gibt es bislang nicht.

"Ich glaube nicht, dass es in erster Linie an logistischen Problemen liegt. Vielmehr fehlt es offenbar am politischen Willen, den Wahlprozess voranzubringen", sagt er.

Die politische Krise wird durch eine umstrittene Verfassungsreform verschärft. Bei einem Referendum am 30. August stimmte eine Mehrheit für Verfassungsänderungen, die die Befugnisse des Präsidenten erweitern und das Parlament von 102 auf 65 Sitze verkleinern. Kritiker bezweifeln die Legitimität des Verfahrens, weil die Reform unter einer Militärführung und ohne ein regulär gewähltes Parlament vorbereitet wurde. Die Opposition hatte zum Boykott der Abstimmung aufgerufen.
Fernando Vaz, Sprecher des Nationalen Übergangsrats, verteidigt die Änderungen. Es habe sich nicht um eine umfassende Neufassung, sondern um eine punktuelle Überarbeitung der Verfassung gehandelt. Die Reform solle helfen, die politische Instabilität des Landes zu überwinden.

Ein Übergang ohne klares Ende
Guinea-Bissau blickt auf Jahrzehnte politischer Instabilität zurück, geprägt von Militärputschen, institutionellen Krisen und wiederholten Unterbrechungen demokratischer Prozesse. Der jüngste Putsch setzt diese Entwicklung fort.

title: Ольга Сумська здивувала, з яким актором погодилась б зіграти інтимну сцену: "Ми б запалили в кадрі"
content_c:
Ольга Сумська здивувала, з яким актором погодилась б зіграти інтимну сцену: "Ми б запалили в кадрі"
Також артистка висловилась, якого фільму їй не вистачає в українському кінематографі.
Українська акторка Ольга Сумська здивувала, з яким відомим актором погодилась б зіграти в інтимній сцені.
Артистка на проєкті «Наодинці з Гламуром» говорить, що їй доводилось раніше втілювати пікантні моменти в кадрі. На такі сцени знаменитість погоджувалась, коли це було виправдано за сценарієм. Однак зараз Ольга Сумська не знімається в таких епізодах. Проте якщо знаменитості ще випаде така нагода, то їй би хотілось, аби її партнером у кадрі був Тарас Цимбалюк.
«З якогось певного моменту я не знімаюся в таких сценах. Хоча колись доволі часто було прописано в сценарії, саме такі еротичні і колоритні епізоди. Вони були виправдані сценарієм, і тільки за цих умов я могла погодитися. Якщо раптом буде така нагода, але я, звісно, соромлюся, але з Тарасом Цимбалюком. Ми могли б запалити в кадрі», — говорить артистка Анні Севастьяновій.
Взагалі, Ольга Сумська вважає Тараса Цимбалюка талановитим актором. Акторка переконана, що особливо йому личать історичні ролі. Артистка говорить, що її колезі чудово б вдалося втілити на екранах отамана Івана Сірка. Тим більше, на думку знаменитості, таких історичних стрічок не вистачає в українському кінематографі.
«Він крутий! Мати такого красеня сьогодні в українському кіно! Він може зіграти будь-якого історичного персонажа. От скажімо отаман Сірко, запорізькі козаки, характерники. Це ж його роль! Продюсери, почуйте! Я розумію, що зараз не на часі, потрібен колосальний кошторис, але про характерників аж прямо душа співає. Отаман Сірко — це Тарас, а я, може, мама чи якась героїня», — коментує артистка.
▶️ Повний випуск «Наодинці з Гламуром» можна подивитися за цим посиланням: РОЗЛУЧЕННЯ, авто в КРЕДИТ та пародія на ТІНУ КАРОЛЬ! Ото, вже ГАЛАСУ НАРОБИЛИ | ЕКСКЛЮЗИВ
Нагадаємо, нещодавно Ольга Сумська поділилась моторошними кадрами атаки на Київ, яку Росія здійснила у ніч проти 22 жовтня. Артистка показала, що пережила.

title: Дмитриев день: традиции
content_c:
Ежегодно 26 октября христиане восточного обряда отмечают День памяти великомученика Димитрия Солунского. Также его еще называют Дмитриев день.
Традиции праздника
В День памяти великомученика Димитрия традиционно завершалась жатва. Хозяйки на праздник пекли блины как символ окончания жатвы. Первый блин предназначался для самого старшего члена семьи, а если он уже умер, то блин оставляли на подоконнике.
Также существовала традиция ходить в храмы в этот день и молиться святому Димитрию. Кроме того, в Димитриев день поминали усопших родных и близких, молясь об упокоении их душ. Хотя по церковному календарю поминовению посвящена Дмитриевская родительская суббота, именно в Дмитриев день для усопших в доме ставили миску с водой, чтобы они могли умыться.
В праздник угощали соседей сладостями, давали милостыню нуждающимся, чтобы те помянули усопших родных и близких.
Молитва в Дмитриев день
Святый и славный великомучениче Христов Димитрие, скорый помощниче и теплый заступниче с верою притекающих к тебе! Предстоя с дерзновением Небесному Царю, испроси у Него прощение согрешений наших и о еже избавитися нам от всегубительныя язвы, труса, потопа, огня, меча и вечныя казни. Моли благость Его, еже ущедрити град сей, обитель сию и всякую страну христианскую.
 
Выпроси у Царя Царствующих на враги победу и одоление православным христианам, всей державе православной мир, тишину, твердость в вере и преспеяние во благочестии; нам же, чтущим честную память твою, испроси благодатное укрепление на дела благая, да благоутробное Владыце нашему Христу Богу зде творяще, сподобимся молитвами твоими наследовати Царствие Небесное для вечнаго прославления Его со Отцем и Святым Духом. Аминь!

title: Займання українського Ан-124 "Руслан" у Японії: що кажуть у компанії "Антонов"
content_c:
Займання українського Ан-124 "Руслан" у Японії: що кажуть у компанії "Антонов"
  - Author, Віталій Червоненко
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 2 хв
22 жовтня у японському аеропорту Chubu Centrair сталося займання частини конструкції українського транспортного літака Ан-124-100 "Руслан" авіакомпанії "Авіалінії Антонова".
Спочатку про це повідомили японський мовник NHK та авіаційний акаунт FL360aero в мережі Х. Згодом факт інциденту підтвердили ВВС News Україна у пресслужбі АТ "Антонов".
"АТ "Антонов" наразі утримується від надання коментарів щодо зазначеного інциденту до встановлення всіх обставин події та отримання офіційно підтверджених результатів відповідних перевірок", - йдеться у заяві пресслужби АТ "Антонов" для ВВС.
За даними японських медіа, загоряння сталося під час приземлення транспортного літака.
Видання NHK вказує, що через інцидент злітно-посадкову смугу закривали на 15 хвилин, після чого вона відновила роботу.
Міністерство землі, інфраструктури, транспорту і туризму Японії з'ясовує подробиці інциденту.
За даними адміністрації аеропорту та міністерства, близько 19:20 22 жовтня було підтверджене загоряння частини фюзеляжу вантажного літака, який здійснював посадку на злітно-посадкову смугу аеропорту. Літак на певний час зупинився на смузі, але невдовзі самостійно її залишив.
Руслани за кордоном та інцидент у Лейпцигу
ДП "Антонов" повідомило, що у зв'язку з неможливістю виконання міжнародних авіарейсів з України, п'ять літаків типу Ан-124-100 "Руслан" тимчасово базуються в аеропорту Лейпцигу. Вони здійснюють важливі перевезення в інтересах України.
Влітку цього року в аеропорту Лейпцига стався інцидент. У ніч проти 5 серпня аеропорт частково призупиняв роботу через загрозу вибуху. Поруч із південною злітно-посадковою смугою виявили підозрілий об'єкт, його знайшли в безпосередній близькості від українського вантажного літака Ан-124 "Руслан".
Дрон був споряджений вибуховим пристроєм.
За даними місцевих ЗМІ, БПЛА влучив у крило українського вантажного літака Ан-124, але не здетонував. Про це 10 серпня повідомляє Die Zeit з посиланням на аналіз записів камер спостереження аеропорту.
Оглядачі вказували, що за цією атакою могла стояти Росія.
Посол України в Німеччині Олексій Макеєв заявив в ефірі Welt TV: "Хто ще міг би стояти за цим, як не Росія?"
Однак Росія інцидент не коментувала.

title: Російська дронова атака на Житомир травмувала дев'ятьох людей і пошкодила цивільну інфраструктуру – Нацполіція
content_c:
Війська РФ у четвер атакували Житомир ударними безпілотниками, внаслідок чого дев'ятеро людей дістали травми та зафіксовані пошкодження об'єктів цивільної інфраструктури, повідомила Патрульна поліція України у п'ятницю.
"Учора ворог атакував Житомир безпілотниками. Унаслідок обстрілу дев'ятеро людей травмовані, серед них – двоє дітей... Пошкоджено об'єкти цивільної інфраструктури", – йдеться у повідомленні відомства у телеграм-каналі.
За даними правоохоронців, жертв унаслідок ворожого удару вдалося уникнути. Спільно з іншими екстреними службами було надано необхідну допомогу постраждалим.
Джерело: https://t.me/patrolpolice_ua/14763

title: Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack
content_c:
Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack
- Published
The condition of Helen Haines, the Australian MP hit by a car five days ago in north-east Victoria, has improved from critical to serious but stable.
The independent MP, 65, had both her legs amputated after what authorities say was a deliberate attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on Monday.
In the latest update on Saturday morning, the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne said Haines was in a serious but stable condition, the first improvement since she was airlifted there.
Her alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, was arrested shortly after the incident and has since appeared in court on three charges.
The politician's husband, Phil Haines, said on Wednesday that the "horrendous incident" had caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind" were "in good shape".
Nugent, who was arrested moments after he allegedly drove his Toyota LandCruiser into the MP, appeared in court to face three charges: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official.
Police said more charges might be laid, including attempted murder.
His lawyer said his client had "mental health concerns" but did not give any further detail.
Victoria Police has said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police, remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established.
Investigators are looking into whether drug use or medication played a part in the incident.
Nugent's family has said they were long-time friends with Haines.
Shortly after the alleged attack, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told ABC television that there had been a "rise in temperature" and "too much shouting, not enough discourse" in Australia.
Haines, known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action, entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife.

title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets
content_c:
Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets
- Published
The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have received suspended prison sentences after they admitted to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.
Anthony Lee used "inside information" emerging from a private meeting called by then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to bet on the general election date months before it took place, Southwark Crown Court heard.
Lee and his wife Laura stood to win more than £23,000 had their cheating not been uncovered, the court heard.
Lee was sentenced to 10 months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, while his wife was sentenced to four months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for a year.
Amy Hind, a former Tory party employee who was working as an NHS business support manager, was also sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for a year, after previously pleading guilty to cheating on the date of the election.
Judge Tony Baumgartner, sentencing the three of them, said their conduct "risked undermining" the confidence the public has in the Conservative Party "as an institution", "undermining trust in the democratic process" and the "integrity of the gambling system".
The trio were among several people charged with betting offences by the Gambling Commission.
The trials of other defendants will take place next year and in 2028.
Former Conservative MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.
'Profit for themselves'
Sunak's decision to call a general election for July 2024 was a surprise to many, including several Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.
The court heard that Sunak held a private Downing Street meeting on 10 March of that year to discuss possible dates.
Neither Lee nor his wife attended the meeting, but the couple began betting online on the election being held in July or between July and September, the court heard.
Prosecutor Zoe Johnson said: "Although not at Number 10, the overwhelming inference is that Anthony Lee was receiving inside information as the meeting went on and was acting upon it."
She added: "Together they were using it to make a profit for themselves."
Lee placed or tried to place 71 bets during the period, while his wife placed eight and attempted a ninth, the court heard.
Baumgartner described Anthony Lee as a "central figure" in the preparation of the general election, who sat at a group of desks within Tory HQ known as the "God Pod".
Representing Lee, barrister Richard Pratt said his client did not concretely know the working date of the election, saying it "still represented a gamble from his point of view".
The barrister told the court: "It was always possible the prime minister could change his mind."
Pratt said there "wasn't any direct manipulation" by the defendant.
Laura Lee worked for the Tories as their "head of international" and had been selected as the party candidate for Bristol North West for the election.
Baumgartner said she had no involvement in the election planning and her access to information "came predominantly" from her husband.
The court heard Hind's husband Anthony worked as a deputy digital director for the Conservatives but did not place any bets himself.
Baumgartner said Hind's husband "was party to emails relating to the forthcoming general election and was one potential source of your inside information".
The judge later said "someone else who worked within the heart of CCHQ" could have given her the "highly confidential" information.
The court heard Hind placed four bets and made three further unsuccessful attempts to place bets. The unsuccessful attempts were for £767, £700 and £750.
The judge described Hind's bets as a "clear departure from your previous betting history", noting: "Before the present offending, your largest stake had been £10.50, and only seven of your 3,399 recorded selections involved a stake of that amount."
'Justice has been served'
Neither of the defendants have previous convictions and they are all of good previous character, the court heard.
Baumgartner described them all as having expressed remorse for their actions.
The trio are now subject to a 12-month prohibited activity requirement, banning them from accessing or using online gambling websites or applications.
Anthony Lee was ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and pay more than £6,600 in compensation to a betting company, while Laura Lee must carry out 40 hours of unpaid work and pay £4,265.
Hind was ordered to complete 50 hours of unpaid work.
Katharine Diamond, General Counsel of regulators the Gambling Commission, reacted to the sentencing of the trio by saying "justice has been served".
She described the case as "a first of its kind" and said it demonstrated the commission's "commitment to protecting the integrity of betting markets".

title: Island inflation rate rises to 3%, figures show
content_c:
Island inflation rate rises to 3%, figures show
- Published
The annual rate of inflation in Jersey rose to 3% in September, according to new figures.
Jersey's retail price index (RPI) rose 0.2 percentage points since June when it was 2.8%.
Statistics Jersey said increases in the cost of household services, alcoholic drinks and food made the most notable contributions to annual rate of inflation.
It said there were also "substantial increases" in the price of some fuels, with heating oil and other fuels increasing by 47.7% across the year, while petrol and oil increased by 22.7%. It said food prices increased by 3.5% and housing costs by 0.2%.
Statistics Jersey said this quarter the island's headline inflation rate was 0.6 percentage points lower than the UK's CPIH, a measure of inflation that includes housing costs, which stood at 3.6%.
It said housing costs made the largest contribution to the RPI - this group includes public and private rentals, as well as mortgage interest payments, parish rates and maintenance and repair costs.
Statisticians said global energy markets remained affected by conflict in the Middle East.

title: Helen Haines’s condition improves days after losing both legs from alleged attack
content_c:
Independent MP Helen Haines’s condition has been downgraded to serious but stable after she lost both legs following an alleged attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria on Monday afternoon.
The Alfred hospital in Melbourne provided an update on Haines’s condition on Saturday morning.
“The patient is in a serious but stable condition at The Alfred on Saturday morning,” a spokesperson for the hospital said.
Haines, the federal MP for the Victorian seat of Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon. Surgeons were trying to save her right leg but both legs had to be amputated due to the seriousness of her injuries.
The MP’s husband, Phil Haines, provided an update at the Alfred hospital on Wednesday, saying “both her heart and her mind are in good shape.”
“I think when we reflect and talk about and think about Helen, the two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind,” he said.
“Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person. Incredibly supportive of all around her – her family, her community, anybody she comes across. And her mind. She has the sharpest intellect.”
Police on Tuesday charged Brendan Nugent, 43, from nearby Tarrawingee with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official. Police have since charged him with two additional offences – cultivating and possessing cannabis – according to court documents.
Nugent appeared at the Wangaratta magistrates court on Wednesday and did not apply for bail.
On Friday, an update on Haines’s social media accounts said her staff were working to reopen her electorate offices next Thursday.
 
 
 “What happened on Monday has deeply affected Helen’s family and all of her staff. Many of us witnessed the incident and some were among the first to come to her aid,” the post read.
“As Helen takes the time she needs to recover, we will take time to look after ourselves and one another, too. Healing will take time, and we ask for your understanding as we navigate the days and weeks ahead.”
Haines’ staff said they had been overwhelmed with kindness shown by the local community in Indi and across Australia and the globe. They said more than $730,000 had been raised for Save the Children in Haines’ honour after her husband directed people to donate to the special appeal as his wife recovered.
“We are deeply moved by the extraordinary generosity of so many people,” the post read.
The alleged attack on Haines has reverberated through Australian politics, prompting conversations about the temperature of political debat, security risks for MPs and mental health services in regional Victoria.
WA Police charged a 56-year-old man after allegedly threatening staff and wielding nunchucks at the electoral office of the the state’s local government minister, Hannah Beazley, days after the alleged attack on Haines.
A community vigil was held for Haines in Wodonga on Wednesday evening after it was revealed the MP had lost both her legs following Monday’s alleged attack.
Haines’s predecessor as the federal member for Indi, Cathy McGowan, said on the sidelines of the event the community was grappling with “mixed emotions”.

title: EU leaders to press Burnham to pay more towards Ukraine’s defence
content_c:
EU leaders will press Andy Burnham at a summit in Brussels to contribute more to Ukraine’s defence effort in 2027.
EU officials argue that the UK, Canada and Japan should do more to support Ukraine, but entreaties to these G7 countries for extra financial aid at recent international meetings have not been answered, Brussels says.
The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, will call on the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, to contribute to Ukraine’s looming financial shortfall at an EU-Canada summit in Montreal next week.
A similar request to the British prime minister will be made when he meets von der Leyen and the European Council president, António Costa, for a long-awaited EU-UK summit on 20 November in Brussels. It comes as the UK chancellor, John Healey, prepares for his first budget next week, weighing numerous calls for more spending against the rising cost of government borrowing and a darkening economic outlook.
Healey said earlier this month he was “working on different ways we can step up support for Ukraine – military, diplomatic and economic”.
Ukraine says it faces a €70bn (£58bn) funding shortfall in 2027 to pay for its defence and civilian needs.
The EU and its member states are paying for 80% of Ukraine’s financial needs, according to the commission, which considers a “fair” EU share to be two-thirds, with the remaining third covered by other allies. “We will continue to lead, but we urgently need other partners to step up,” von der Leyen told reporters last week, without naming countries.
The EU last year agreed a €90bn loan for Ukraine, intended to cover two-thirds of Kyiv’s funding in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia escalates its attacks, dragging the war into its fifth winter, Ukraine’s costs continue to spiral.
EU officials have prioritised non-EU G7 countries, above all the UK, Canada and Japan. But they are now casting the net wider and may look to Switzerland, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand to promise additional aid to Ukraine.
The British government says it has committed £25bn to Ukraine, including £16bn in military aid.
The UK is Ukraine’s fourth largest donor, behind the US, Germany and France, according to the Kiel Institute’s Ukraine Support Tracker. But the picture changes when the UK’s share is weighted to GDP. The UK was assessed by the Kiel researchers as spending 0.86% of national income to support Ukraine, compared with 1.1% from France and 1.5% from Germany. These three large European economies spent significantly less than the Nordics and Baltics, such as Denmark (4.2%) and Estonia (3.8%). The UK is more in line with France and Germany when their contribution to EU programmes is stripped out.
The UK government has been contacted for comment.
The European Commission declined to comment on specific countries, but referred to a recent statement: “We always said that we cannot walk this alone … therefore our partners in general must step up.”
Ukraine will be one of several issues on the agenda at the EU-UK summit, where leaders are expected to conclude three agreements: a food and animal health (SPS) deal to reduce Brexit paperwork; the linkage of the EU and UK emissions trading schemes (ETS) to protect British industry from European carbon taxes; and a youth mobility scheme to enable 18- to 30-year-olds to live, work, travel and study across both sides of the Channel.
In a positive sign for British negotiators, the European Commission proposed deferring the question of university tuition fees, one of the last big sticking points. The UK would like to charge EU students at British universities the international rate, about four times higher than the domestic fee. The EU, where many officials are alumni of British universities, wants to return to the pre-Brexit status quo, when EU students paid home rates.
Commission officials have proposed resolving this thorny question in technical talks within six months of the 20 November summit, rather than risk derailing the high-profile leaders’ meeting. But senior EU sources are confident they still have leverage on the issue, as the SPS and ETS deals will not come into force until there is a youth mobility agreement acceptable to the European side, including on tuition fees.
“The three elements are a sort of gift to the UK, but not a massive gift,” an EU diplomat said, adding that the EU would still have clout in the negotiations over the fees. “The leverage is that the UK needs this [the other agreements].” UK hopes to strike economic security agreements with the EU, to avoid British industry becoming collateral damage of Europe’s defensive measures against China, are seen as another source of leverage.
But a second diplomat said there was no consensus among the EU’s 27 member states on postponing the tuition fees question until after the summit: “There is no clear majority saying ‘let’s drop it now for six months’,” they said.

title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
content_c:
With repeat attacks, Russia has put Kyiv on war's front line
October 23, 2026
Until a few months ago, life was relatively peaceful in Kyiv when compared with the situation near the war's front lines elsewhere in Ukraine. Now, as Russia expands its attacks on the capital, Kyiv has increasingly become a front-line city.
With too few shelters for the 4 million residents of Kyiv, subway stations double as makeshift dormitories. Starting at about 10 every night, people create sleeping areas with mattresses and small tents. Children snuggle up to adults; pets seek comfort from their owners or find a spot among strangers between the cold walls.
"We're alive," Halyna told DW, holding her 5-year-old son, Roman, close. "We've been lucky once again." Most evenings — even when no air-raid siren has sounded — she takes the boy to the nearest subway station. Her apartment is located in the Lukyanivka district, which Russia has systematically targeted over the war's four years and eight months.
'These sick monsters don't care who they kill'
In September, 14-year-old Daniel Umanskyj was doing homework in his room when a Russian drone struck the apartment building in the central district of Pechersk. A neighbor named Vlad happened to be in the hallway with his daughter at the time of the strike. "We were late that day — and this saved our lives," Vlad said. "Daniel's death is a tragedy." He added: "These sick monsters don't care who they kill." Flowers have been planted in front of the damaged apartment building in memory of Daniel.
Russia also targets places where children gather. In early October, a drone struck a school building in southwestern Kyiv. Fortunately, pupils and teachers were already in shelters at the time.
"We've been teaching all the pupils in person because we have a large shelter that can accommodate more than 500 students," Valentyna Chorna, the school's principal, told DW. As there is enough space in the shelter for everyone, students in the first through ninth grades are able to go to school, she said.
Danger at home, at school — everywhere
Whether classes take place depends not only on the decision of the parents and the school administration: It also depends on whether shelters are available and how long the air-raid siren continues to sound. If an alarm sounds in the morning while children are still at home, they may not be able to go to school that day.
"This is an enormous burden for parents," said a colleague from the DW bureau in Kyiv, whose daughter attends school. "You have to go to work — and the child stays home alone."
"Even the walk to school is dangerous because an air-raid alarm can go off at any time," she said. Her daughter attends a school not far from the Antonov aircraft factory. "One day she texted me: ‘You can't imagine what a huge explosion that was!'" she said. "I don't know if something was shot down or if there was a strike somewhere." She added: "Things like that really scare children." And staying home brings its own risks.
In September, a Russian drone struck their building. The apartment itself wasn't damaged, and her daughter was at school that morning, but it was another reminder of just how much survival has become a matter of luck. When an air-raid siren sounds, no one knows who will be spared, she said.
Kyiv's population persists
Russia's attacks have become deadlier in 2026. According to the military administration in Kyiv, 140 people were killed in the capital during the first eight months of the year, compared with 172 for all of 2025. If this trend continues, 2026 could become Kyiv's deadliest year since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022.
Attacks on warehouses have led to shortages in supermarkets on a scale not seen since the early months of the war. At the end of September, emergency power outages resumed in Kyiv. The subway was paralyzed by a Russian attack. Given the strikes on the energy infrastructure, it is unclear how the capital can reliably supply residents with heat, electricity and water during the upcoming winter.
Despite Russia's attempts to render Kyiv uninhabitable, 72% of the city's residents said in September that they are prepared to endure the war for as long as necessary, the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology reported in early October. The authorities are striving to maintain normal life in the city, where the curfew has been shortened and now runs from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.
Some facilities have even been allowed to continue operating during "yellow" alerts. During "red" alerts, however, people must immediately seek shelter: This could mean ballistic missiles, cruise missiles or massive combined attacks.
This article was originally written in Ukrainian.
description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

title: Israel startet «Anti-Terror-Operation» im Westjordanland
content_c:
Naher Osten Israel startet «Anti-Terror-Operation» im Westjordanland
Als Reaktion auf einen Angriff im Westjordanland mit zwei getöteten Soldaten hat Israel eigenen Angaben zufolge einen Antiterroreinsatz im Raum Hebron gestartet. »Die Kräfte haben begonnen, das Gebiet gezielt, präzise und umfassend zu durchsuchen, um Terrorinfrastruktur und Waffen ausfindig zu machen und zu beseitigen«, hieß es am späten Abend in einer gemeinsamen auf der Plattform Telegram veröffentlichten Erklärung der israelischen Armee und des Inlandgeheimdiensts Schin Bet.
Der gemeinsame Einsatz von Armee, Geheimdienst, Grenzpolizei und Zivilverwaltung sei auf das Gebiet beschränkt, aus dem die Terroristen operierten, und werde voraussichtlich mehrere Tage dauern.
Am Freitagmorgen hatte es einen Angriff mit Schusswaffen in der Nähe von Hebron im Westjordanland gegeben. Dabei wurden laut Angaben des israelischen Militärs zwei Soldaten getötet und drei weitere verletzt. Die beiden mutmaßlich palästinensischen Täter aus Hebron wurden getötet. Die Sicherheitskräfte hätten dadurch einen »schweren Anschlag« verhindert, sagte Israels Ministerpräsident Benjamin Netanyahu.
Hebron: Bagger zerstört angeblich illegale Bauwerke
Foto: Mamoun Wazwaz \ apaimages / APAimages / IMAGO
Auf X teilte er mit, er habe Militär und Sicherheitskräfte angewiesen, die Stadt Hebron sofort abzuriegeln und zusätzliche Sicherheitsmaßnahmen zu ergreifen, um Terroranschläge aus dem Westjordanland zu verhindern.
Am Dienstag findet in Israel die Parlamentswahl statt (mehr zu den Wahlen hier ). Der Konflikt mit den Palästinensern ist ein wichtiges Wahlkampfthema. Rechte Politiker versuchen bei ihrer Wählerschaft zu punkten, indem sie ein hartes Vorgehen gegen palästinensische Gewalt versprechen. Die zunehmenden Angriffe radikaler israelischer Siedler auf Palästinenser im Westjordanland thematisieren sie dagegen kaum.
Armee: Abriss illegaler Bauwerke
Die Armee teilte am Abend weiter mit, zusätzlich würden Maßnahmen ergriffen, um die Sicherheitslage in dem Gebiet zu verbessern. Dazu gehörten der Abriss illegaler Bauwerke, die am Ort des Zwischenfalls eine mögliche Sicherheitsbedrohung darstellen könnten. Die Sicherheitskräfte führten derzeit in Dutzenden Orten im Westjordanland Antiterroreinsätze durch.
Seit Beginn des Einsatzes könnten Bewohnerinnen und Bewohner des betroffenen Gebiets über drei ausgewiesene Ausgänge nach Befragung das Gebiet verlassen, hieß es weiter. Zu den Antiterrormaßnahmen zähle auch die Abriegelung der Gebiete Hebron und Halhul sowie die Einrichtung von Straßensperren.
UN-Generalsekretär Guterres zeigt sich besorgt
UN-Generalsekretär António Guterres zeigte sich unterdessen »zutiefst besorgt« über die Abriegelung von Hebron sowie über Berichte von Hausabrissen und möglichen Vertreibungen, wie sein Sprecher in New York mitteilte. »Diese Absperrungen schränken die Bewegungsfreiheit der Palästinenser, ihren Zugang zu grundlegenden Dienstleistungen und ihre Lebensgrundlage erheblich ein«, sagte der Sprecher.
Israel hat im Sechstagekrieg 1967 unter anderem das Westjordanland und Ostjerusalem erobert und hält dieses Gebiet seither besetzt. Dort leben heute inmitten von drei Millionen Palästinensern rund 700.000 israelische Siedler.
Die Lage im besetzten Westjordanland hat sich seit dem Hamas-Massaker am 7. Oktober 2023 in Israel und dem dadurch ausgelösten Gazakrieg noch einmal verschärft. Nach Angaben des palästinensischen Gesundheitsministeriums wurden im Westjordanland seitdem mehr als 1100 Palästinenser bei israelischen Militäreinsätzen, bewaffneten Auseinandersetzungen und eigenen Anschlägen getötet.
Aber auch die Gewalt radikaler israelischer Siedler gegen Palästinenser hat stark zugenommen. Dem israelischen Militär wird immer wieder vorgeworfen, nicht entschlossen genug gegen solche Angriffe vorzugehen oder sogar mit den Siedlern zu kooperieren.
description: Seit dem Abend geht Israels Armee eigenen Angaben zufolge gegen Terroristen im Westjordanland vor. Damit reagiere man auf den Angriff vom Morgen, heißt es. Am Dienstag wird in Israel gewählt.
