title: Argentina drops investigation into President Milei over crypto fraud
content_c:
Argentina drops investigation into President Milei over crypto fraud
- Published
A criminal investigation into Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister's links to a cryptocurrency scandal has been dropped.
The case against Milei and his sister Karina Milei was dismissed by federal judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi at the request of prosecutors, court records show.
The Argentinian president had denied promoting the newly launched cryptocoin $Libra , which collapsed shortly after he mentioned it in a social media post in February 2025.
He said he had acted "in good faith" when the cryptocurrency rose in value before crashing and causing huge losses for the majority of its investors. Milei is yet to respond to news of the case being dropped.
Dismissing the case, the judge said "the reported events do not fall under a legal category", and concluded that no "criminally relevant deception" had been proven.
Accusations of fraud arose when Milei posted on X, formerly Twitter, about the $Libra coin, which he said at the time would help fund small businesses and start-ups.
The cryptocurrency's price subsequently shot up when the Argentine president shared a link to buy it.
But, within a few hours, he deleted his post and the crypto nosedived in value, losing investors most of their money.
It led opposition members of Congress to plan impeachment proceedings, while some online accused Milei of a "rug pull" - where promoters of a cryptocurrency draw in buyers, only to stop trading activity and make off with the money raised from sales.
The Argentinian president, though, insisted: "I didn't promote it, I merely shared it" in an interview with local media Todo Noticias'.
The presidential office insisted that Milei was in no way involved in the development of $Libra and announced that the Anti-Corruption Office would determine if the president had acted improperly.
Milei himself defended deleting his post, saying that at the time he did not know "the details of the project and after learning about it, I decided not to continue promoting it".
And, in a TV interview, he insisted that those who invested in $Libra had done so "voluntarily" and knew of the risks.

title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner
content_c:
Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner
- Published
A police force has still not received the £2m it was promised by the government in the wake of a car crash that led to the deaths of seven people, including two police officers, the local police and crime commissioner (PCC) says.
Cleveland PCC Matt Storey said Cleveland Police was still waiting for the extra funding promised by the home secretary in August.
Shabana Mahmood pledged the cash in light of challenges faced by the force following the deaths, which followed a pursuit on the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on 22 August. Five young men were also killed.
The Home Office said the force would receive the £2m it had been promised by the end of November.
During the fatal crash, a Volkswagen Passat in which the five young men were travelling hit an oncoming marked Cleveland Police vehicle on the dual carriageway near Middlesbrough at about 03:39 BST.
Officers PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died at the scene.
The occupants of the VW Passat, which was travelling the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, and 17-year-olds Theo Rae and Cole Robert Worthy - were also killed.
On the morning of the crash, Cleveland Police said it received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously around the town and a Volvo XC60 had been seen ramming properties.
Further arrests were subsequently made in connection with organised crime, including the following weekend after another vehicle ramming.
Storey called for the immediate release of the £2m but also said policing costs linked to the crash, which had led to the arrests of 50 people so far, were now forecast to exceed £5m.
"These are exceptional and unavoidable costs arising from utterly tragic and devastating circumstances," he said.
"They are not costs that should be borne locally or met from existing policing budgets."
The PCC also criticised the lack of a "substantive" communication from the government about Cleveland Police's long-term funding.
Storey said the current police funding model, which Mahmood had previously committed to reviewing, disadvantaged the Teesside force.
He said the upcoming Budget was a chance to "align resources more fairly with demand" and "place Cleveland on a sustainable footing".
The 50 arrests have come as part of a wider police operation against organised crime following the crash.
Fifteen people have been charged - 13 men and two women ranging in age from 19-45.

title: Jordon Steele-John’s position remains in limbo as Greens prepare for moment in spotlight
content_c:
More than a week after allegations that Greens senator Jordon Steele-John had behaved inappropriately towards women made headlines, his position in the party remains in limbo and its new leader’s handling of the issue in question.
David Shoebridge’s first major challenge at the helm of the federal Greens came earlier this month when the Nine newspapers reported a three-page letter had been sent to him urging an independent investigation into Steele-John.
It referred to secondhand allegations that the Western Australian senator had acted inappropriately towards women between 2017 and 2025.
As a progressive party that prides itself on taking such matters seriously and fairly, it made sense that Shoebridge announced the 32-year-old’s leave amid an independent probe into the claims.
But the process quickly became more complicated. Days later, a defiant Steele-John rejected the allegations against him, denied he agreed to take leave from parliament, and accused an internal faction within the WA Greens of playing “nasty political games” in its decision to release the letter to the media.
Steele-John said he made a public statement because he didn’t want his silence on the letter’s claims to be perceived as guilt.
While Shoebridge insists Steele-John agreed to take leave, he acknowledges he alone does not have the power to force the senator to do so.
Only if two-thirds of the party room – or more than seven members – decided to expel him in a secret ballot would Steele-John have to comply.
Such a move would be nuclear. Even if the WA Greens’ independent investigation clears him of any wrongdoing, Steele-John’s standing in the party room would be shattered.
The week ahead under scrutiny
Senate estimates is a time for members of the upper house to have their moment in the spotlight. For the Greens, it’s a chance to extricate answers about government policies from carefully trained bureaucrats to drive home a political point.
With the NDIS undergoing major changes between now and the decade’s end, Steele-John, who is championed and well-liked within the disability community as the party’s disability spokesperson, will not attend.
Steele-John issued a statement late Friday saying he had explored attending digitally, but had “been informed that would also be unacceptable”.
“As such I have decided not to return next week and will instead focus on the independent and timely investigation I hope is soon commenced by the Greens WA,” Steele-John said.
For many supporters within and outside the Greens, the optics of allowing a federal party member accused of sexual misconduct – even though a complainant has not directly come forward to make those allegations – to continue public duties would have been a tough pill to swallow. Particularly as the “manosphere” phenomenon and backlash against the #MeToo movement gain momentum in mainstream society.
The question over whether the allegations were politically motivated by adversaries of Steele-John looking to gain advantage in the state’s pre-selection is a part of the equation.
But the fact remains that the rumours have persisted over the senator’s time in office. Even if they are malicious, as Steele-John contends, the simpler option would still be to stand aside and settle them while they are investigated.
The decision over whether to force Steele-John to take leave will be as much about Shoebridge’s leadership as it is about the party’s processes.
The party room, and its membership more broadly, prides itself on being a movement based on consensus decision-making.
Shoebridge will need the support of the party room to take the expulsion route. How he handles this issue will also set the tone for the rest of his leadership and, depending on his actions, could prompt an ugly battle with Steele-John.
It’s a quagmire – politically, legally and ethically.
There are unlikely to be any winners.

title: This man has quit Badenoch’s increasingly hard-right Tory party – others should be brave enough to do the same | Polly Toynbee
content_c:
The chair of the London Assembly, Andrew Boff, resigned this week from the Conservative party after 53 years of membership. He quit after being blocked from entering the race to be Tory candidate for London mayor because he supports the European convention on human rights (ECHR), putting him at odds with Kemi Badenoch’s hardline position.
Messages of support for one of the capital’s longest-serving Conservative politicians quickly poured in from fellow Tories. Gavin Barwell, Theresa May’s Downing Street chief of staff, has backed Boff, warning Badenoch that others would follow him over the ECHR edict. But the rest sent messages privately, not daring to reveal themselves under a leadership that doesn’t tolerate dissent. In an interview last year, Badenoch decreed that rebels “should not and cannot stand as a Conservative candidate” if they do not agree with leaving the ECHR. She also bars anyone supporting net zero.
When Boff applied, for the seventh time, to be considered as Conservative candidate for London mayor, he didn’t really expect to be selected – but nor did he expect to be summoned to be told he was barred from entering the race. In a statement he pointed to the fact that Winston Churchill helped found the ECHR after the second world war, arguing “it was never a leftwing project” but a “safeguard against arbitrary government”. What’s more, he points out to me, the “convention doesn’t even mention asylum seekers”, Badenoch’s main justification for leaving the treaty.
The time may come, he warned, when extremists win an election on an even smaller vote share than Labour’s 34% in 2024 – and overturn all human rights legislation without the protections the ECHR affords. “That’s what authoritarian governments do,” Boff said. But he insisted that the committee, which vets Conservative candidates, didn’t listen. “They just repeated the same tropes, that activist judges are using the ECHR against parliament.”
Now he is free of the party straitjacket, Boff is planning to stand for London mayor as an independent, allowing him to say what he thinks about Badenoch.
He complains to me that the energy and resources that should promote the party “all go to promoting Kemi, Kemi, Kemi”. Thinking well of her in 2015, he says he had encouraged her to stand for the London assembly, where she served until 2017 before being elected to parliament. He says he found her “lazy and combative”.
Few will be surprised by Boff’s departure. But many will be wondering what took him so long. He was ejected from the Tory conference in 2023 for quietly heckling the then home secretary Suella Braverman’s speech, accusing her of homophobia and transphobia. “It is a signal to people who don’t like people who are LGBT+,” Boff, who is gay, said at the time as he condemned her speech as “trash”. Boff said that Braverman “was basically vilifying gay people and trans people by this attack on LGBT ideology”.
He was not alone in voicing criticism over the party’s direction. The former Tory MP Robert Buckland, fellow one-nationer and director of the Tory Reform Group, hurried out to defend Boff after his ejection from the conference, saying heckling was “part of the democratic debate” and that his treatment by security staff was “heavy-handed”.
Buckland was among the many one-nationers who lost their seat at the 2024 general election. But that traditional strand of Conservatism has not vanished – nor have those who used to vote for the Tories but now turn to the Liberal Democrats or simply boycott the ballot box.
Boff’s views represent a growing centre-right moderate strand that has been expelled or silenced under Badenoch’s leadership. Facing this hostile climate, one nation Tories have gone to ground in parliament; but outside the Commons, Prosper UK, a centrist Tory grouping led by the former mayor of the West Midlands, Andy Street, and the former Scottish Tory leader Ruth Davidson quietly gains strength.
Its mission statement is to win back moderate voters who snubbed the Conservatives at the last general election, and this message seems to have struck a chord, with the group attracting nearly 30,000 supporters since its launch in January.
It is worth examining Boff’s views, as many Conservatives who have signed up to Prosper UK are likely to share them. He calls himself a Thatcherite, strongly opposing Labour’s renationalisation plans, backing low taxes and a small state. He voted for Brexit, believing the words of the likes of Daniel Hannan, who claimed “absolutely nobody is talking about threatening our place in the single market”. But instead the Tories delivered a hard Brexit after what he calls an “atrocious” campaign.
Times have changed; as the political analyst Peter Kellner pointed out this week, Britain’s pro-Brexit majority has literally died out. Any so-called betrayal of the referendum is only betraying the dreadful legacy of the departed.
If the Conservative party has any future as a government, it won’t be under its present leader. A small bounce for improved performance in parliament will never overcome Badenoch’s growing distance from voters, including those who should be natural Tories.
Boff may be a throwback to an irretrievable, more moderate Conservative brand, like that of the Macmillan era – a voice from the good old days when traditional party allegiances were clearly defined. That won’t be easy: already there are gloating Spectator-aligned Tories who say that the party is better off without the likes of Boff, or any real concession to centrism. But we should have a care. The success of a respectable right matters to all in the left bloc of progressive parties, too. A centre right is needed to fight off the dark forces of the hard right and worse, here and across Europe. That Overton window framing politics needs a firm shunt towards a more rational debate on our future in Europe – and on saving the planet.

title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
content_c:
Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
October 23, 2026
US first lady Melania Trump helped broker a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia in the city of Oleshky, the White House announced Friday. The localized truce, according to the White House, is slated to begin on October 29.
What do we know so far about the ceasefire deal in Oleshky?
The Ukrainian city occupied by Russia on the frontline of the war faces a humanitarian crisis and only around 2,000 people still live there. Prior to the war, the city had a population of around 24,000.
Oleshky has been under blockade since 2025 and was first occupied when Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The city is located in southern Ukraine, just 9 kilometers (around 5.6 miles) from the major city of Kherson.
"Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water," Melania Trump said in a statement. "The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks."
Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, thanked the first lady for securing the deal.
"Under our agreement: first a ceasefire will be put in place; second, humanitarian aid will be delivered to Oleshky; and third, civilians will be allowed to move freely out of Oleshky," Lubinets said in a video message posted on Telegram. "The operation will be carried out gradually and is extremely challenging to implement."
Russia also confirmed the agreement and said it will halt fire earlier than what the White House announced at 0400 local time (0100 GMT) on October 27.
According to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights, residents in Oleshky say Russian occupying forces prevented them from leaving the city. Oleshky residents also say Russia has used civilians to shield military positions in the city — a war crime under international humanitarian law.
Fresh Ukraine talks expected in Abu Dhabi next month
The ceasefire deal in Oleshky comes as US, Ukrainian and Russian negotiators are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi next month to discuss ending the war.
"The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course," Zelenskyy told the US conservative Hudson Institute think tank.
In comments to Russian state news outlet TASS, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov also said preparations are underway for a three-way meeting in mid-November. Russian President Vladimir Putin said security would be a main topic for the Abu Dhabi talks.
"That is the security of both countries, Russia and Ukraine, after there has been a transition to a peace settlement," Peskov said.
The Kremlin spokesperson said Russia only sees the Europeans at the table during a later stage in the talks. European leaders such as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz have said Europe must be involved in future Ukraine peace talks.
"It is clear that the architecture of European security cannot be discussed without other participants," Peskov added.
US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated at Zelenskyy, and is pressuring him to "make a deal."
Trump has blamed Ukraine for rising diesel prices in the US, as the US-Israeli war against Iran has caused the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and drove up the cost of gas at the pump for American consumers.
Trump has backed a deal to buy diesel from Russia to lower prices at fuel pumps, drawing criticism from Ukraine. The Kremlin said Friday that the first tanker of Russian diesel has set sail for the US despite the backlash from Ukraine.
Ukraine still dealing with Starshield issues as Trump defends Musk
Most recently, there has been controversy that tech billionaire Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of the Starshield military communications system that Ukraine relies on, possibly with the backing of Trump.
Trump has denied that he ordered restrictions on Starlink. He also defended Musk in comments to reporters on Friday and said, "Elon will never do anything wrong."
"You know, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn't make any difference," Trump said. "I guess the bottom line, he put it back."
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy and Ukraine said Friday that the system was still being throttled in Ukraine.
"It works, but it's still limited," Zelenskyy told US broadcaster ABC News.
A source in Ukraine's Defense Ministry told AFP news agency and other news outlets that Ukrainians were witnessing "instances of signal loss" when using Starshield.
"There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted," the source added.
Edited by: Sean Sinico

title: Wadephul zieht positive Bilanz nach Außenministertreffen in Istanbul
content_c:
Wadephul bei Außenministertreffen Neues Gesprächsformat, besseres Krisenmanagement?
Beim ersten Treffen dieser Art hat Außenminister Wadephul mit sieben anderen Chefdiplomaten aus Europa und Nahost in Istanbul über Kriege und Konflikte beraten. Seine Bilanz: positiv. Künftig soll es regelmäßige Treffen geben.
Das Gesprächsformat ist neu, die Gesprächspartner höchst unterschiedlich. Doch alle sind von den Entwicklungen am Persischen Golf betroffen, wenn auch in unterschiedlicher Weise. Europa spürt es mehr an der Zapfsäule, andere auf dem Teller.
Mit Blick auf Iran und die von ihm unterstützten jemenitischen Huthi machte der deutsche Außenminister Johann Wadephul unmissverständlich klar:
                
                
                Wir sprechen hier mit einer Stimme, wenn wir sagen, genug ist genug. Iran und die Huthi erpressen die Weltwirtschaft mit ihren Angriffen auf die internationale Schifffahrt. Sie sind verantwortlich für die Destabilisierung des Mittleren Ostens, für humanitäre Krisen im Jemen und für Ernährungskrisen im globalen Süden.
Gemeinsame Initiative Deutschlands und der Türkei
Der Versuch, Bewegung in die festgefahrenen Konflikte zu bringen, war eine gemeinsame Initiative Deutschlands und der Türkei. Während Deutschland, Großbritannien und Frankreich auf Erfahrungen in den Atomverhandlungen mit Iran zurückgreifen können, pflegt die Türkei enge Beziehungen vor allem zu Saudi-Arabien und Pakistan, mit denen sie gerade ein Verteidigungsbündnis ins Leben gerufen hat. Gleichzeitig ist sie gemeinsam mit den Europäern in der NATO.
Außenminister Hakan Fidan sprach deshalb auch von einem richtigen Format, um den Krisen und Konflikten in der Region zu begegnen:
                
                
                Wir leben in einer Welt, in der Ereignisse im Nahen Osten Europa und Ereignisse in Europa den Nahen Osten beeinflussen. Eine Unterbrechung der Getreidelieferketten Russlands und der Ukraine im Schwarzen Meer kann zu einer Lebensmittel-Krise in Ägypten führen. Die Sperrung der Straße von Hormus verursacht eine Energiekrise und steigende Preise in Europa. Daher ist es nur normal, dass diese beiden Formate nun zusammenkommen und zusammenarbeiten.
Appell an Putin
Wie ein zynischer Gruß in Folge des russischen Angriffskriegs auf die Ukraine versenkte kurz vor Beginn des Treffens eine Drohne ein Handelsschiff vor der rumänischen Küste - der siebte Angriff auf ein Frachtschiff dort in diesem Monat.
Wadephul appelliert an Russlands Machthaber Wladimir Putin zu erkennen, "dass es Zeit ist, den Einstieg in den Ausstieg zu finden, dass es Zeit ist, die schon seit langem ausgestreckte Verhandlungshand der Ukraine zu ergreifen, dass es Zeit ist, die unsäglichen Angriffe auf Getreidelieferungen im Schwarzen Meer zu beenden, mit denen er wissentlich eine weitere Krise im globalen Süden anzettelt".
Positive Bilanz
Wadephul betonte, alle acht Staaten, die an dem Treffen beteiligt waren, seien willens, ihren Beitrag zu leisten, damit Sicherheit und Stabilität in der Region und die Freiheit der Seewege wiederhergestellt werden. Es war das erste Gespräch in diesem Format, und auch wenn es keine konkreten Beschlüsse gab - es war erfolgreich, so die Bilanz des deutschen Chefdiplomaten:
                
                
                Alle haben gespürt, dass es eine Dringlichkeit gibt, jetzt miteinander zu sprechen, natürlich Meinungen auszutauschen, aber auch gemeinsame Positionen miteinander zu formulieren. Und das ist besser gelungen, als wir zu hoffen gewagt hatten. Es ist so gut gelaufen, dass wir vereinbart haben, uns ab jetzt regelmäßig zu treffen.
Das nächste Treffen soll in Deutschland stattfinden. Er werde bald mit den Vorbereitungen beginnen, sagt Wadephul.

Gleichzeitig ist sie gemeinsam mit den Europäern in der NATO.
Außenminister Hakan Fidan sprach deshalb auch von einem richtigen Format, um den Krisen und Konflikten in der Region zu begegnen:
                
                
                Wir leben in einer Welt, in der Ereignisse im Nahen Osten Europa und Ereignisse in Europa den Nahen Osten beeinflussen. Eine Unterbrechung der Getreidelieferketten Russlands und der Ukraine im Schwarzen Meer kann zu einer Lebensmittel-Krise in Ägypten führen. Die Sperrung der Straße von Hormus verursacht eine Energiekrise und steigende Preise in Europa. Daher ist es nur normal, dass diese beiden Formate nun zusammenkommen und zusammenarbeiten.
Appell an Putin
Wie ein zynischer Gruß in Folge des russischen Angriffskriegs auf die Ukraine versenkte kurz vor Beginn des Treffens eine Drohne ein Handelsschiff vor der rumänischen Küste - der siebte Angriff auf ein Frachtschiff dort in diesem Monat.
Wadephul appelliert an Russlands Machthaber Wladimir Putin zu erkennen, "dass es Zeit ist, den Einstieg in den Ausstieg zu finden, dass es Zeit ist, die schon seit langem ausgestreckte Verhandlungshand der Ukraine zu ergreifen, dass es Zeit ist, die unsäglichen Angriffe auf Getreidelieferungen im Schwarzen Meer zu beenden, mit denen er wissentlich eine weitere Krise im globalen Süden anzettelt".
Positive Bilanz
Wadephul betonte, alle acht Staaten, die an dem Treffen beteiligt waren, seien willens, ihren Beitrag zu leisten, damit Sicherheit und Stabilität in der Region und die Freiheit der Seewege wiederhergestellt werden. Es war das erste Gespräch in diesem Format, und auch wenn es keine konkreten Beschlüsse gab - es war erfolgreich, so die Bilanz des deutschen Chefdiplomaten:
                
                
                Alle haben gespürt, dass es eine Dringlichkeit gibt, jetzt miteinander zu sprechen, natürlich Meinungen auszutauschen, aber auch gemeinsame Positionen miteinander zu formulieren. Und das ist besser gelungen, als wir zu hoffen gewagt hatten. Es ist so gut gelaufen, dass wir vereinbart haben, uns ab jetzt regelmäßig zu treffen.
Das nächste Treffen soll in Deutschland stattfinden. Er werde bald mit den Vorbereitungen beginnen, sagt Wadephul.

title: News kompakt: Atommüll-Endlagerung in Finnland kann starten
content_c:
News kompakt: Atommüll-Endlagerung in Finnland kann starten
23. Oktober 2026
In Finnland kann das weltweit erste Endlager für hochradioaktive nukleare Abfälle in Betrieb gehen. Die finnische Regierung erteilte die entsprechende Genehmigung. Wann in der unterirdischen Anlage der erste Atommüll eingelagert wird, steht noch nicht fest. Nach Angaben des Entsorgungsunternehmens Posiva sind zunächst weitere Tests und Inspektionen nötig. Der Betrieb solle aber bald aufgenommen werden.
Die Bauarbeiten für das Endlager in Eurajoki im Südwesten des nordeuropäischen Landes hatten vor 22 Jahren begonnen. Das Tunnelsystem befindet sich in 1,9 Milliarden Jahre altem, festem Grundgestein. Es bietet Kapazität für 6500 Tonnen strahlenden Abfall. In der Anlage sollen abgebrannte Brennelemente aus den fünf finnischen Kernreaktoren gelagert werden, die noch Jahrtausende lang hochradioaktiv sind.
Tausende Venezolaner fordern Machado-Rückkehr
Erstmals seit fast zwei Jahren sind in Venezuela Anhänger der Opposition landesweit auf die Straße gegangen. Tausende forderten freie Wahlen und politische Veränderungen. Zu den Kundgebungen in der Hauptstadt Caracas und mehreren anderen Städten hatte die Bewegung Vente Venezuela der im Exil lebenden Oppositionsführerin und Friedensnobelpreisträgerin María Corina Machado aufgerufen. Die Demonstranten forderten unter anderem deren Rückkehr in das südamerikanische Land.
Ohne Machados Beteiligung waren vor gut einer Woche Verhandlungen zwischen Vertretern der Regierung von Übergangspräsidentin Delcy Rodríguez und der Opposition gestartet. Dabei bekräftigten beide Seiten ihren Willen, Präsidentenwahlen in Venezuela abzuhalten.
Mindestens 16 Tote bei Beben in Tibet
In der autonomen Region Tibet im Westen Chinas laufen nach einem schweren Erdbeben Such- und Rettungseinsätze. Bislang wurden nach Angaben chinesischer Staatsmedien 16 Tote geborgen. Die Zahl der Verletzten stieg demzufolge auf 54.
Im Kreis Baqing hatte in der Nacht zum Freitag (Ortszeit) die Erde mit einer Stärke von 7,0 gebebt. Das teilte die chinesische Erdbebenwarte mit. Der Herd des Bebens lag in einer Tiefe von rund 10 Kilometern. Es sind die bisher stärksten Erdstöße in diesem Jahr in China. In der Region Tibet kommt es häufig zu Erdbeben. Sie werden durch die Kollision der indischen und der eurasischen Kontinentalplatte verursacht.
Mutmaßlicher Spion kommt vor Ermittlungsrichter
Ein am Donnerstag im Bundesland Brandenburg im Osten Deutschlands unter Spionageverdacht gefasster Ukrainer wird an diesem Freitag einem Ermittlungsrichter am Bundesgerichtshof in Karlsruhe vorgeführt. Der Richter entscheidet, ob der Verdächtige in Untersuchungshaft kommt. Die Bundesanwaltschaft wirft dem Mann vor, für einen Nachrichtendienst Russlands militärisch relevante Informationen gesammelt zu haben. Dazu habe er unter anderem Kontakte in die europäische Rüstungsindustrie genutzt, so der Verdacht. Laut deutschem Strafgesetzbuch drohen dem Ukrainer bis zu zehn Jahre Freiheitsstrafe.
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz wertete die Festnahme als Erfolg. Zugleich warnte Merz vor weiterer Spionage. Die Aktivitäten des russischen Geheimdienstes in Deutschland seien unverändert hoch.
IStGH: "Sacharow-Preis wichtiges Signal"
Der Internationale Strafgerichtshof (IStGH) in Den Haag hat dem Europa-Parlament für den Sacharow-Preis gedankt. Die Auszeichnung habe gerade in dieser Zeit eine besondere Bedeutung. Das Gericht und seine Mitarbeiter seien derzeit mit beispiellosen Herausforderungen konfrontiert wie etwa Sanktionen. Der IStGH steht vor allem vonseiten der USA unter Druck. US-Präsident Donald Trump verhängte Strafmaßnahmen gegen Richter und Ankläger und kündigte an, das Gericht vom internationalen Finanzsystem abzuschneiden.
Die Entscheidung für den diesjährigen Preisträger war am Donnerstag von EU-Parlamentspräsidentin Roberta Metsola verkündet worden. Mit dem Sacharow-Preis soll der Einsatz für Demokratie und Menschenrechte gewürdigt werden. Die Verleihung findet am 16. Dezember in Straßburg statt. Der mit 50.000 Euro dotierte Preis ist nach dem sowjetischen Physiker, Menschenrechtler und Friedensnobelpreisträger Andrej Sacharow benannt.
Klimawandel gefährdet Großteil der Korallenriffe
Weltweit sind laut einer Prognose der Weltnaturschutzunion (IUCN) fast alle Korallenriffe vom Aussterben bedroht. Grund ist der fortschreitende Klimawandel. In den kommenden 50 Jahren bestehe für 96 Prozent der Korallenriffe in flachem Wasser ein extrem erhöhtes Risiko, heißt es in der Analyse. Es war die erste weltweite Untersuchung dieser Art. Die IUCN schätzte für ihre Prognose den Zustand und die Entwicklung von Korallenriffen vor den Küsten von mehr als 80 Ländern und Gebieten ein.
Korallen sind besonders anfällig für die Auswirkungen der globalen Erwärmung. In wärmeren Ozeanen sterben die Mikroorganismen, die ihnen ihre leuchtenden Farben verleihen und sie mit Nahrung versorgen. Laut IUCN-Generaldirektorin Grethel Aguilar ist es noch nicht zu spät, die Korallenriffe zu retten. Nötig dafür seien ehrgeizige Ziele bei der Reduzierung von Treibhausgasen sowie umfangreiche Schutz- und Wiederherstellungsmaßnahmen für die Riffe wie etwa die Ausweitung von Meeresschutzgebieten.
AR/gri/jj (afp, dpa, rtr, efe, ifax)
Dieser Artikel wurde um 9.00 Uhr (MESZ) erstellt und wird nicht weiter aktualisiert.

title: Яке церковне свято в Україні 25 жовтня
content_c:
Яке церковне свято в Україні 25 жовтня
Що за церковне свято святкують в Україні за новим і старим календарем і кому моляться віряни — читайте в матеріалі ТСН.ua.
25 жовтня (7 листопада), в православному календарі день пам’яті мучеників Маркіяна та Мартирія. Маркіян і Мартирій жили в IV столітті в Константинополі. Вони служили при Константинопольській церкві за часів патріарха Павла Сповідника. Маркіян був читцем, а Мартирій — іподияконом. Обидва вирізнялися побожністю, освіченістю та відданістю християнському вченню.
Святі були близькими до патріарха Павла, який захищав православне вчення про Божество Ісуса Христа. У той час Церква переживала складний період через поширення аріанства — вчення, яке заперечувало повноту Божества Сина Божого. Релігійні суперечки супроводжувалися політичним тиском, вигнаннями духовенства та переслідуваннями тих, хто залишався вірним православній вірі.
Коли патріарха Павла усунули від служіння та відправили у вигнання, Маркіян і Мартирій не відмовилися від своїх переконань. Вони продовжували підтримувати православне вчення й залишалися відданими церковному служінню, попри небезпеку.
Їхня позиція викликала невдоволення противників патріарха. Святим погрожували, намагаючись змусити їх зректися своїх переконань і перейти на бік тих, хто заперечував православне вчення.
Однак Маркіян та Мартирій не піддалися тиску. Вони розуміли, що вірність Христу для них важливіша за особисту безпеку, спокій і земні блага.
За церковним переданням, Маркіяна та Мартирія засудили до страти через їхню непохитну відданість християнській вірі. Їх стратили в Константинополі, імовірно близько 355 року, за правління імператора Констанція II.
Перед смертю святі не зреклися своїх переконань і залишилися вірними Христу до кінця. Їхній подвиг став прикладом духовної стійкості для християн, які переживали переслідування та церковні розколи.
Після смерті Маркіян і Мартирій були вшановані як святі мученики. Їхню пам’ять зберегла Церква, наголошуючи на мужності, вірності та готовності захищати істину навіть перед обличчям смерті.
Церковне свято в Україні 25 жовтня за старим календарем
За старим календарем 25 жовтня в Україні вшановували пам’ять святих мучеників Прова, Тараха і Андроніка. За церковним переданням, Пров був римлянином, Тарах — уродженцем Сирії, а Андронік походив зі знатної родини. Їх заарештували за сповідування християнства та намагалися змусити зректися віри. Попри катування й погрози, мученики залишилися непохитними та прийняли смерть за Христа.
Прикмети 25 жовтня
- Якщо 25 жовтня морозно — незабаром може настати стійке похолодання.
- Якщо йде дощ — очікували сирої та похмурої погоди найближчими днями.
- Якщо небо затягнуте хмарами — зима може бути близько.
Що не можна робити 25 жовтня
У цей день також закликають бути милосердними й не залишати без підтримки тих, хто її потребує. Вважається, що допомога ближнім, присвячена світлій пам’яті померлих, має особливе духовне значення. Милостинею можуть бути не лише гроші, а й продукти, конкретна допомога, добре слово або щире побажання. За народними віруваннями, кожен такий прояв доброти Бог бачить і приймає як вияв любові та молитву за тих, кого вже немає серед живих.
Що можна робити 25 жовтня
У народній традиції 25 жовтня відоме як день Дідівських плачів. Цю дату пов’язують із вшануванням померлих і збереженням пам’яті про рідних, які відійшли у вічність. За звичаєм, цього дня відвідують кладовища, наводять лад на могилах близьких, ставлять запалені свічки та звертаються в молитвах до Бога за упокій їхніх душ. Особливо доброю справою вважається впорядкувати занедбане поховання, навіть якщо воно належить незнайомій людині.

За церковним переданням, Пров був римлянином, Тарах — уродженцем Сирії, а Андронік походив зі знатної родини. Їх заарештували за сповідування християнства та намагалися змусити зректися віри. Попри катування й погрози, мученики залишилися непохитними та прийняли смерть за Христа.
Прикмети 25 жовтня
- Якщо 25 жовтня морозно — незабаром може настати стійке похолодання.
- Якщо йде дощ — очікували сирої та похмурої погоди найближчими днями.
- Якщо небо затягнуте хмарами — зима може бути близько.
Що не можна робити 25 жовтня
У цей день також закликають бути милосердними й не залишати без підтримки тих, хто її потребує. Вважається, що допомога ближнім, присвячена світлій пам’яті померлих, має особливе духовне значення. Милостинею можуть бути не лише гроші, а й продукти, конкретна допомога, добре слово або щире побажання. За народними віруваннями, кожен такий прояв доброти Бог бачить і приймає як вияв любові та молитву за тих, кого вже немає серед живих.
Що можна робити 25 жовтня
У народній традиції 25 жовтня відоме як день Дідівських плачів. Цю дату пов’язують із вшануванням померлих і збереженням пам’яті про рідних, які відійшли у вічність. За звичаєм, цього дня відвідують кладовища, наводять лад на могилах близьких, ставлять запалені свічки та звертаються в молитвах до Бога за упокій їхніх душ. Особливо доброю справою вважається впорядкувати занедбане поховання, навіть якщо воно належить незнайомій людині.

title: «Мы готовы»: Зеленский о том, согласится ли Украина на заморозку войны по линии фронта
content_c:
Президент Украины Владимир Зеленский заявил, что готов заключить соглашение о прекращении войны с Россией на условиях заморозки боевых действий по существующей линии соприкосновения. В то же время Украина не будет признавать временно оккупированные территории российскими и не согласится добровольно покинуть дополнительные территории. Об этом Зеленский сказал в интервью ABC News.
«Мы готовы остановить эту войну как можно скорее», — сказал он.
В то же время на вопрос, готова ли Украина ради мира отказаться от 25% своей территории, Зеленский ответил отрицательно. По его словам, такое условие означало бы, что украинские войска должны сами выйти со всей территории Донбасса, которую они до сих пор контролируют.
«Мы не соглашались отдать 25% нашей территории», — подчеркнул он.
Зеленский отметил, что Украина никогда не признает оккупированные территории российскими.
«Я слышал такие предложения: признать, что временно оккупированная территория станет российской. Конечно, мы не согласимся...», — заявил украинский президент.
Ранее Зеленский в эфире американского телеканала Fox News говорил, что согласился бы на мирное соглашение, предусматривающее замораживание боевых действий и сохранение контроля над 75% страны. По его словам, при таких условиях Украина потребует гарантий безопасности от партнеров.
В июне президент Украины уже заявлял, что готов заморозить линию фронта и «зафиксировать» ситуацию, чтобы начать мирные переговоры о завершении войны в Украине. Он пояснил, что такой путь — хотя он ему и не нравится — является самым быстрым и позволит наконец «перейти в дипломатическую плоскость».
Россия тогда отвергла это предложение.

title: Глава МЗС Польщі спростував заяву Маска про збагачення на допомозі США Україні
content_c:
Міністр закордонних справ Польщі Радослав Сікорський спростував твердження генерального директора компанії SpaceX Ілона Маска щодо нібито збагачення українських еліт на багатомільярдній допомозі американських платників податків, наголосивши на припиненні фінансування Києва з боку США торік і закупівлі американського озброєння коштом європейських держав.
"Ні, Ілоне, США припинили фінансування України ще минулого року. Насправді американські компанії заробляють на американській зброї, за яку платимо ми, європейці. Чим більше ви втручаєтеся в нашу політику і чим більше граєте в політику зі своїми продуктами, тим більше ви шкодите своєму бренду", – написав очільник польського МЗС у X.
Своєю чергою Маск напередодні опублікував у соцмережі X допис, у якому заявив про істотну різницю в стимулах між українськими елітами та громадянами, стверджуючи, що представники влади нібито збагатилися на сотнях мільярдів іноземної допомоги на тлі мобілізації населення до війська. Американський мільярдер також висловив припущення, що частина коштів платників податків США повертається через схеми відмивання грошей для фінансування політичних кампаній у Сполучених Штатах, чим він пояснив підтримку України з боку окремих американських політиків.
Водночас головний міжнародний кореспондент телеканалу ABC News Джеймс Лонгман у соцмережі X повідомив із посиланням на президента України Володимира Зеленського, що поточна швидкість роботи терміналів Starlink залишається недостатньою для запуску українських оборонних безпілотників. За даними журналіста, за останні три місяці Сполучені Штати передали Україні лише 24 ракети-перехоплювачі до систем протиповітряної оборони Patriot, тоді як лише за минулий тиждень російські війська випустили по території України 80 балістичних ракет.

title: White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
content_c:
White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
- Published
US First Lady Melania Trump has "successfully secured" a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, the White House has said.
It said the truce in the "front-line war city on the brink of disaster" without medicine, food and clean water would begin on 29 October.
Ukraine and Russia confirmed the deal was agreed to evacuate residents and deliver aid. They both said their forces would stop firing at 02:00 GMT on 27 October.
Oleshky was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Trapped between Ukrainian positions across the Dnipro River and Russian forces to the east, residents have recently resorted to eating garden weeds to survive.
The White House statement said Melania Trump and one of her representatives had worked "directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire".
"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require," she is quoted as saying.
"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive co-ordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine."
Melania Trump added that Oleshky residents "have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks" and that "without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible".
The statement did not say how long the ceasefire would be in place for.
Davyd Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads President Volodymyr Zelensky's party in parliament, later said "an operation to unblock the settlement of Oleshky and its surroundings will begin in the near future".
"To achieve this goal, a ceasefire will be achieved in the near future, as announced by the First Lady of the United States, Melania Trump," he said.
In Russia, President Vladimir Putin's spokesman confirmed that, "those who wish to do so will be able to leave this settlement".
Last month, some of the remaining Oleshky residents told the BBC harrowing accounts of how they were surviving in the city that was being constantly shelled and cut off from food and water.
They said that children remaining in wider Oleshky were suffering from malnutrition, a lack of medical services and were "degrading" without access to education.
Many also told the BBC there was only one hospital partially operational, opening a few days a week to perform critical amputations.
The local population was living under a "full blockade" by Russian forces, according to Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.
Ukraine says it has attempted to deliver supplies to the area but has not had success in recent months.
The Kremlin in September acknowledged that Oleshky was facing "a critical situation" and "problems with supplies of food and medicine", but added that "Russia's military was working to resolve them" and blamed Kyiv.
Oleshky was home to 24,000 people before Russia's full-scale invasion. Now Ukraine estimates that some 6,000 people remain in the city and its surrounding areas, including 200 children.
It is also one of a number of settlements where thousands of people lost their homes to a massive flooding caused by the collapse of Nova Khakovka Dam in 2023. Ukraine and its allies accused Russia of blowing up the dam, while Russia blamed Ukraine.
While the US first lady is relatively lower profile than some of her predecessors - and only occasionally seen at White House events - she has become involved in addressing humanitarian issues stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war.
In August 2025, Melania Trump penned a letter to Putin, telling him it was "time to protect children and future generations worldwide".
Although she did not mention Ukraine by name, just days later at the White House Zelensky handed over a letter from his wife Olena, thanking her for her efforts on children.
In a rare public appearance in October the same year, the US first lady said that Putin had answered directly in writing and that her representatives were working with the Russian president's team to repatriate Ukrainian children from Russia and vice versa.
Some 34 children have reportedly been returned since 2025, including five this July.
According to US President Donald Trump, his wife has also privately expressed scepticism about Putin and his desire to achieve peace.
"I'd get home, I'd say, 'First lady, I had the most wonderful talk with Vladimir. I think we're finished'," Trump said in July last year.
"And then I'll turn on the television, or she'll say to me one time, 'Wow, that's strange because they just bombed a nursing home.'"
Additional reporting by Olga Malchevska

title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says
content_c:
Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says
- Published
Andy Burnham said military aircraft will be used to tackle wildfires as he tries to ensure the UK is "on the front foot" following a summer of devastating blazes.
Civilian fire services in all four nations will be able to request the support of the Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M planes to fight wildfires on tough terrain such as remote moorland and steep hillsides.
As he hosted the UK's first summit on wildfires, the prime minister outlined initial steps to "improve our response" after the country "lived through a summer that we've never seen before".
Burnham said this also includes better equipment for firefighters and improved land management to stop fires from spreading.
After a record-breaking summer, the government's "wildfire resilience summit" in Liverpool on Friday discussed how to prevent, respond to and recover from such blazes.
There have been 1,350 wildfires in England and Wales this year, an all-time high and up by more than 300 on last year and more than 1,000 on 2024, according to figures from the National Fire Chiefs Council.
Records for the number of reported wildfires were also broken in 2022 and 2025 - but the UK's Climate Change Committee has warned the risk will rise in the coming decades.
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said this was the first time the RAF's Chinooks and the four-engine A400Ms were being equipped to tackle wildfires. Some areas struggled with no air assistance in the summer.
RAF Chinook crews have already helped respond, external to wildfires in Cyprus.
In addition to military aircraft, the government said it would also spend £45m on wildfire-specific personal protective equipment for firefighters on the ground.
It is lighter than current firefighting equipment which is designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, the government added.
Ministers are also pledging a £25m scheme from April 2027 to April 2029 to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they are natural firebreaks, and financial support for farmers to fireproof their land such as by digging ponds.
"The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high," a briefing ahead of the summit said, following a temporary ban on disposable BBQs.
Burnham met fire chiefs, local leaders and experts from tech companies at the summit, also attended by Communities Secretary Angela Rayner.

Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says
- Published
Andy Burnham said military aircraft will be used to tackle wildfires as he tries to ensure the UK is "on the front foot" following a summer of devastating blazes.
Civilian fire services in all four nations will be able to request the support of the Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M planes to fight wildfires on tough terrain such as remote moorland and steep hillsides.
As he hosted the UK's first summit on wildfires, the prime minister outlined initial steps to "improve our response" after the country "lived through a summer that we've never seen before".
Burnham said this also includes better equipment for firefighters and improved land management to stop fires from spreading.
After a record-breaking summer, the government's "wildfire resilience summit" in Liverpool on Friday discussed how to prevent, respond to and recover from such blazes.

title: France to deploy 70,000 police on Saturday to prevent civil unrest
content_c:
France will deploy about 70,000 police around the country on Saturday as the government seeks to prevent more civil unrest after some of the worst street violence in years erupted on the fringes of cost-of-living protests last weekend.
The interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said on Friday the security forces would include elite units usually used for counter-terrorism operations and hostage rescues, adding that there had been social media calls for violence from “ultra-left” groups.
“We are not talking about a peaceful, friendly demonstration,” Nuñez told reporters after a meeting of senior ministers and officials chaired by the president, Emmanuel Macron. “We are ready tomorrow to be extremely firm and not tolerate anything.”
Major museums including the Louvre, Orsay Museum, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais – where a major Cézanne exhibit is on display – are closed Saturday. Art Basel, one of the world’s most prestigious contemporary art fairs, opened to the public Friday, but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organisers to cancel the weekend program.
Parisian shopkeepers have been barricading their stores all week. Near Place de la République in Paris, one of last weekend’s hotspots, a bank branch and other businesses were boarded up with wooden panels to deter potential looters.
Macron and his government are struggling to get on top of a crisis that has caught it off guard six months before presidential elections to choose his successor. The government has admitted it “lost control” over widespread rioting on Saturday.
Largely peaceful demonstrations were hijacked by groups of determined rioters, degenerating into rampant violence and extensive looting in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities. In Limoges, the town hall was set on fire and partly destroyed.
“We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all who commit violence,” Nuñez said, adding that besides 10,000 more police, the operation would include water cannon, armoured vehicles, mounted police, helicopters and drones.
Demonstrations are expected in several other countries this weekend, triggered by a broader, continent-wide wave of discontent over declining public services, housing affordability, public sector budget cuts and the spiralling cost of living.
Protests over related grievances have been called for Saturday in Milan, Rome and Turin in Italy; in Vienna, Austria; and in Madrid, Barcelona and other cities in Spain, as well as in Lisbon and Porto in Portugal, Dublin in Ireland and Tirana in Albania.
Protests are expected across France on Saturday, although several cities have banned demonstrations or forced them to change their planned routes to protect shops and public buildings, and forecast heavy rain and high winds could dampen turnout.
The centres of Lyon and some other large cities will be off-limits to protesters, while authorities in Paris authorised a union march along a limited route in the east of the capital between the Places de la Bastille and Nation that will avoid the city centre.
But requests for rallies in Paris organised by France’s main student union, UNEF, and the gilets jaunes movement, whose nationwide protests rocked France in 2018 and which plans 600 small-scale events around France on Saturday, were refused.
UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and dilapidated facilities, would go ahead regardless. Several of the best-known cultural institutions in Paris, including the Louvre, said they would close on Saturday.
Authorities in Marseille had also banned all protests, but announced on Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis”. It will be the only authorised protest in the southern Bouches-du-Rhône department.
Unionists and opposition leaders have criticised the government for refusing to allow more rallies on Saturday, a decision being challenged in court in several cities. Marylise Léon of the CFDT union federation accused Macron of an abuse of authority.
“It’s counterproductive because there is a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to,” Léon, the CFDT’s general secretary, told TF1 TV. “It’s not for the president to decide who can legitimately protest.”
La France Insoumise, the radical left party of Jean-Luc Mélenchon, said the government had “crossed the lines that separate a democracy from an authoritarian and police state”, adding that the bans would only “generate more chaos”.
Adding to the tensions, the far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner for next spring’s presidential elections, is due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orléans, drawing thousands of supporters – and leftwing, anti-racist opponents.
Nuñez was due to visit the city on Friday to “inspect the security arrangements” at the request of the prime minister’s office. The justice minister, Gérald Darmanin, said 217 people – half of them first-time offenders – had been jailed since Saturday.
On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, saying gangs of rioters had been mainly responsible for the looting but the worst violence was caused by “ultra-left” groups seeking to “bring down the republic”.
Further stoking disquiet, one person was killed and four others injured – including a 12-year-old girl – in a shooting in the town of Trappes, west of Paris, on Friday in an attack that police said could have been racially motivated.

title: ‘Realistic and reassuring’: UK public ‘responding calmly’ to Be Ready campaign
content_c:
When the UK government launched its “Protect and Survive” public information campaign in 1980 on how to stay alive after a nuclear attack, it was met with a combination of scepticism, disbelief and derision.
The advice included how to build a “fallout room” at home, how to whitewash windows to protect from a blast, and how to store a dead body for up to five days.
You might expect this would have prompted widespread panic, but in fact it led to a political backlash, and was later lampooned on TV and in music.
It shows the risks governments take when launching such campaigns, and the fine balance that must be struck between hammering home a practical message without causing panic – or other unintended reactions.
The government’s new Be Ready campaign is advising the public to stock up on three day’s worth of supplies for use during severe weather or cyber-attacks, so help can be directed to the most vulnerable first.
In a concise, two-page document, it suggests people stock bottled water and non-perishable food for three days, a torch with spare batteries, a wind-up FM radio, a first aid kit and a copy of their passport. To stave off panic buying, it advises people to check their cupboards first and build up items gradually on regular shopping trips.
While there is no evidence the advice has triggered mass panic, the public is clearly responding. Jack Brown, who co-owns Sgt Prepper Shop, which stocks emergency food and survival tools, said he received a month’s worth of orders in the first 24 hours of the Be Ready campaign.
“I thought my phone was glitching or being hacked with the number of orders coming in,” he said.
Brown said the advice seemed sensible and proportionate. Three days was the “sweet spot”, he said, with most everyday emergencies like power cuts, a burst water main or flooding sorted within that timeframe.
It is also “realistic, affordable and fits in a cupboard”, he said, adding that asking people to stock up on a month’s worth of supplies would feel overwhelming and most people would do nothing at all.
A wind-up radio was also a sensible suggestion, and ones with a built-in torch and phone-charging USB port make them “one of the most useful bits of kit you can own”, he said.
Dr Sarita Robinson, associate dean for the school of psychology and humanities at the University of Lancashire, said there was little evidence to suggest these kinds of messaging campaigns cause panic.
“There’s this perception that if we tell people the truth we’re somehow going to panic them and it isn’t the case,” she said.
“When we use accurate messaging about emergency situations, the public will engage with that proactively. It’s when we start to hide information and there’s a void of information, that’s when things can go wrong for government.”
She said Be Ready was “realistic, quite low level, and should be reassuring because it’s basically treating the public like the grownups they are”.
Dan Goss, who runs Start Prepping UK, said traffic to his website was up 700% since news of the campaign emerged in August. He said he was glad to see the subject finally being taken seriously and spoken about in “plain language” by the government, and felt the risk of panic was low.
“The level of uptake required for that would be huge – you would need to have an enormous number of people all take the government’s advice very seriously and all jump on it as a priority,” he said.
“We’re definitely in a phase now where we’re seeing lots of more disruption to people’s lives – not necessarily apocalyptic disasters, but things that have a big impact on small areas, so this advice is very much needed.”
Robinson said the campaign showed how the perception of “prepping” has shifted, especially since the Covid-19 pandemic when most people will remember seeing empty supermarket shelves.
“We did a study during Covid that showed people who did mild levels of prepping, such as having food, masks and hand gel in the house a few weeks before the pandemic, had lower anxiety and depression, and less stress,” she said.
“The government really needs to portray that this is just normal, everyday, very common in other countries, and isn’t wearing a tinfoil hat and building a nuclear bunker in your back garden.”

title: Afghan women could lose one of their last paths to a higher education
content_c:
Afghan women could lose one of their last paths to a higher education
October 23, 2026
"Laila" awoke in the middle of the night for a glass of water, checked her phone almost by accident, and saw an email that made her stomach drop. The US would stop funding the American University of Afghanistan (AUAF), one of the last places women can still study in the country.
Laila said she sat on her bed, staring, her thoughts racing through the past five years and everything she had endured just to get an education.
It had not been easy to find a way to study in Afghanistan after the Taliban outlawed women's education.
The American University campus was already taken over by the Taliban, but she could study secretly through the university's online program. But now that the university is losing its financing, she told DW she and her classmates fear it will shut down entirely. Her name has been changed for safety reasons.
A hidden education for women in Afghanistan
Laila is in her mid-twenties. She studies political science and international studies and is one of around 1,000 enrolled students at the university, three-quarters of them women.
When the Taliban returned to power in August 2021, Laila was studying at another university in Kabul, with just two final exams remaining to finish her semester. Then, in December 2022, the Taliban announced the ban. Laila's degree was left unfinished.
Laila secured a scholarship to AUAF and started over. "Not every girl got that opportunity," she said.
Laila has told few people outside of her family about her online studies. On most days, she stays home for remote lectures, alongside classmates who use aliases and keep their cameras off for security. "I just know their voices," she said.
Laila speaks English with an American accent. She learned it as a child, watching cartoons. In her early twenties, she was learning even more about the world outside Afghanistan and studying foreign governments.
Then on August 14, 2021, Laila's life changed. She and a friend sat in a restaurant in Kabul. They had just finished an exam and wanted to celebrate passing the test by ordering coffee and cake. Suddenly, a man came in, stopped at the entrance, and shouted "Allahu Akbar." He yelled that the mujahideen would always be victorious.
That was the day the Taliban retook power in Afghanistan, they soon forced women out of public life, banning them from many jobs and from attending school and university.
Laila said she recalls losing feeling in her hands or feet. She pulled money from her purse and slammed it on the table without checking the amount. "We all thought maybe this would be the last day that we are alive," she said.
Since then, some of Laila's peers have received threatening calls and messages. Now, whenever she leaves home, she worries that Taliban authorities might search her phone.
"What if they see my emails from my work, from my university?" she said. "It's always in the back of my head that maybe tomorrow it's my turn. Maybe they will detain me."
Even her home isn't safe. Laila said Taliban authorities have entered on several occasions to search their belongings.
Yet, she has continued studying. For all its limitations and risks, the online program offered a chance to graduate.
A place for Afghanistan's 'future leaders'
With the US pulling out as the university's primary funder, Laila said she doubts whether she has the strength to start over.
The American University of Afghanistan was always intended, largely, for women. Before the campus opened in 2006, former US first lady Laura Bush announced that the US had committed millions to support it.
Appearing in Kabul, Bush said the new university would teach "future leaders," particularly women. Women like Laila, who was four years old at the time.
"These are more than just development projects," Bush said at the time. "They also signify the bond between the American and Afghan people. They are symbols of our shared hopes and dreams."
Patrick Fine was Afghanistan mission director at USAID, the now-defunct American development agency. Fine told DW that many at USAID considered the university idea risky. Critics thought training elites was a waste of money.
But the Bush administration saw an opportunity to stabilize a budding democracy, Fine said.
By 2003, the Taliban had been driven from power. US President George W. Bush wanted to foster goodwill for the US-backed interim government that had replaced the Taliban. The university served that goal, and also offered other "facets of advantage" in educating women, training future politicians, and supporting the Afghan economy.
"It really impacted the lives of thousands of Afghan youth," Fine said, referencing alumni. "The organization has managed to achieve that against incredible odds."
Washington pulls the plug
The university continued with US support. But in Washington, that support started to come under question.
The US government suspected the university of mishandling money. In 2016, US inspectors opened an investigation into its finances. By 2018, investigators said they could not tell exactly how it was spending US aid money, because its accounting was so poor.
John Sopko, a former US federal inspector, oversaw that investigation. When DW contacted him for this story, he replied, "I was surprised they were still funding AUAF."
This year, after the funding was pulled, the US State Department Press Office told DW in an email that the move was made given the university's "history of repeated lack of accountability for millions of American taxpayer dollars."
Fine, the former USAID director, rejected the State Department's fraud explanation.
"Those are just smear tactics," he said. He conceded that past audits found the university struggling to keep up with USAID's extensive rules, "but they didn't find major fraud," he said.
"It is still a useful investment, a worthy investment," Fine said, "and the reason for that is that it's one of the few organizations left that is reaching Afghan women."
The US isn't the university's only funder, but it has long covered most of its costs: nearly 90% as of 2018, according to a US report.
The US State Department told DW that the university is "free to identify other funders and partners, so the end of their receipt of American taxpayer money does not necessarily equate to an end to their operations."
But without the $25 million grant the State Department recently refused, the university's future is in doubt.
What is next for women students in Afghanistan?
"I have lost all my motivation and hope," Laila said, adding that each time she prepares for a lecture, she wonders whether there will be another.
Since she learned about the funding cut, she said she's barely left her room. Her curtains are usually closed, and she's lost her appetite. "Maybe I'm so disappointed that I can't even cry about it," she said.
She said she was supposed to have graduated years ago. She was supposed to be making the world a better place. She was supposed to be studying for a master's degree abroad. Now, she's thinking, maybe she'll find a way in five or ten years.
Edited by: Wesley Rahn
description: The US has defunded one of the last universities giving Afghan women the chance to receive an education after the Taliban takeover in 2021. DW spoke with a student who says she's lost hope of ever earning a degree.

The American University campus was already taken over by the Taliban, but she could study secretly through the university's online program. But now that the university is losing its financing, she told DW she and her classmates fear it will shut down entirely. Her name has been changed for safety reasons.
A hidden education for women in Afghanistan
Laila is in her mid-twenties. She studies political science and international studies and is one of around 1,000 enrolled students at the university, three-quarters of them women.
When the Taliban returned to power in August 2021, Laila was studying at another university in Kabul, with just two final exams remaining to finish her semester. Then, in December 2022, the Taliban announced the ban. Laila's degree was left unfinished.
Laila secured a scholarship to AUAF and started over. "Not every girl got that opportunity," she said.
Laila has told few people outside of her family about her online studies. On most days, she stays home for remote lectures, alongside classmates who use aliases and keep their cameras off for security. "I just know their voices," she said.
Laila speaks English with an American accent. She learned it as a child, watching cartoons. In her early twenties, she was learning even more about the world outside Afghanistan and studying foreign governments.
Then on August 14, 2021, Laila's life changed. She and a friend sat in a restaurant in Kabul. They had just finished an exam and wanted to celebrate passing the test by ordering coffee and cake. Suddenly, a man came in, stopped at the entrance, and shouted "Allahu Akbar." He yelled that the mujahideen would always be victorious.
That was the day the Taliban retook power in Afghanistan, they soon forced women out of public life, banning them from many jobs and from attending school and university.
Laila said she recalls losing feeling in her hands or feet. She pulled money from her purse and slammed it on the table without checking the amount. "We all thought maybe this would be the last day that we are alive," she said.
Since then, some of Laila's peers have received threatening calls and messages. Now, whenever she leaves home, she worries that Taliban authorities might search her phone.
"What if they see my emails from my work, from my university?" she said. "It's always in the back of my head that maybe tomorrow it's my turn. Maybe they will detain me."
Even her home isn't safe. Laila said Taliban authorities have entered on several occasions to search their belongings.
Yet, she has continued studying. For all its limitations and risks, the online program offered a chance to graduate.
A place for Afghanistan's 'future leaders'
With the US pulling out as the university's primary funder, Laila said she doubts whether she has the strength to start over.
The American University of Afghanistan was always intended, largely, for women. Before the campus opened in 2006, former US first lady Laura Bush announced that the US had committed millions to support it.
Appearing in Kabul, Bush said the new university would teach "future leaders," particularly women. Women like Laila, who was four years old at the time.
"These are more than just development projects," Bush said at the time. "They also signify the bond between the American and Afghan people. They are symbols of our shared hopes and dreams."
Patrick Fine was Afghanistan mission director at USAID, the now-defunct American development agency. Fine told DW that many at USAID considered the university idea risky. Critics thought training elites was a waste of money.
But the Bush administration saw an opportunity to stabilize a budding democracy, Fine said.
By 2003, the Taliban had been driven from power. US President George W. Bush wanted to foster goodwill for the US-backed interim government that had replaced the Taliban. The university served that goal, and also offered other "facets of advantage" in educating women, training future politicians, and supporting the Afghan economy.
"It really impacted the lives of thousands of Afghan youth," Fine said, referencing alumni. "The organization has managed to achieve that against incredible odds."
Washington pulls the plug
The university continued with US support. But in Washington, that support started to come under question.
The US government suspected the university of mishandling money. In 2016, US inspectors opened an investigation into its finances. By 2018, investigators said they could not tell exactly how it was spending US aid money, because its accounting was so poor.
John Sopko, a former US federal inspector, oversaw that investigation. When DW contacted him for this story, he replied, "I was surprised they were still funding AUAF."
This year, after the funding was pulled, the US State Department Press Office told DW in an email that the move was made given the university's "history of repeated lack of accountability for millions of American taxpayer dollars."
Fine, the former USAID director, rejected the State Department's fraud explanation.
"Those are just smear tactics," he said. He conceded that past audits found the university struggling to keep up with USAID's extensive rules, "but they didn't find major fraud," he said.
"It is still a useful investment, a worthy investment," Fine said, "and the reason for that is that it's one of the few organizations left that is reaching Afghan women."
The US isn't the university's only funder, but it has long covered most of its costs: nearly 90% as of 2018, according to a US report.
The US State Department told DW that the university is "free to identify other funders and partners, so the end of their receipt of American taxpayer money does not necessarily equate to an end to their operations."
But without the $25 million grant the State Department recently refused, the university's future is in doubt.
What is next for women students in Afghanistan?
"I have lost all my motivation and hope," Laila said, adding that each time she prepares for a lecture, she wonders whether there will be another.
Since she learned about the funding cut, she said she's barely left her room. Her curtains are usually closed, and she's lost her appetite. "Maybe I'm so disappointed that I can't even cry about it," she said.
She said she was supposed to have graduated years ago. She was supposed to be making the world a better place. She was supposed to be studying for a master's degree abroad. Now, she's thinking, maybe she'll find a way in five or ten years.
Edited by: Wesley Rahn

title: Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger nennt Deutschlandticket für Gelegenheitsfahrer »spannende Idee«
content_c:
Steffen Bilger Verkehrsminister nennt Deutschlandticket für Gelegenheitsfahrer »spannende Idee«
Bundesverkehrsminister Steffen Bilger hält den Vorschlag eines neuen bundesweit geltenden Tickets für gelegentliche Fahrten in öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln für eine »spannende Idee«. »Denn ein einfacher Zugang zu den Angeboten von Bus und Bahn ist wichtig. Die Digitalisierung kann dazu neue Möglichkeiten schaffen«, sagte der CDU-Politiker dem »Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger«.
Zwar hätten die Verkehrsminister der Länder das Thema vorerst bis zur nächsten Verkehrsministerkonferenz vertagt, da es noch Fragen zu den finanziellen Auswirkungen sowie zur konkreten Umsetzung zu klären gebe. »Als Bundesverkehrsministerium beobachten wir die weitere Entwicklung daher mit Interesse«, sagte Bilger.
Nordrhein-Westfalen und Hamburg hatten den Vorschlag zur Einführung eines »bundesweiten elektronischen Gelegenheitstarifs« im Regionalverkehr gemacht, er wurde jedoch bereits zum Auftakt der Konferenz der Verkehrsminister von der Tagesordnung genommen und nicht diskutiert.
Die Idee eines Tickets für Gelegenheitsfahrten sollte eine Ergänzung zum Deutschlandticket sein. Per Smartphone sollten dabei Fahrten registriert werden und der günstigste Tarif automatisch berechnet werden.
In Nordrhein-Westfalen gibt es bereits ein Modell, bei dem per App ein- und ausgecheckt wird. Die monatlichen Kosten sind dabei auf 63 Euro gedeckelt, dem aktuellen Preis für das Deutschlandticket. Der Tarif gilt jedoch nur innerhalb des Bundeslands.
Oliver Krischer (Grüne), der Verkehrsminister aus Nordrhein-Westfalen, hatte klargestellt, dass es bei dem jetzt vorgeschlagenen bundesweiten Digitalticket für Gelegenheitsfahrer keine Preisobergrenze geben soll. »Wir wollen bundesweit natürlich keinen Preisdeckel, das würde das Deutschlandticket konterkarieren«, sagte Krischer zum Abschluss der Verkehrsministerkonferenz in Hohenschwangau in Bayern.
Krischer sprach von einem entscheidenden Zukunftsthema für den ÖPNV. Es solle nicht nur ein Deutschlandticket für die Vielfahrer geben, sondern auch ein digital bundesweit gültiges Ticket für diejenigen, die gelegentlich den ÖPNV nutzten.
Lesen Sie die Analyse zum Ticket für Gelegenheitsnutzer: Ein Deutschlandticket zum Ein- und Auschecken, gedacht für wenige Fahrten im Monat – das schlagen Nordrhein-Westfalen und Hamburg vor. Es gibt noch andere Ideen, wie der ÖPNV-Tarif attraktiver würde .
description: Mit dem Handy in Bus und Regionalbahn einchecken und am Ende den besten Tarif bekommen – auch wenn man sich nicht auskennt. Für Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger ist die Idee eines neuen Tickets nicht vom Tisch.

title: Anti-Terror-Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt nach tödlichen Schüssen bei Paris
content_c:
Tödlicher Angriff auf Passanten Anti-Terror-Behörde ermittelt nach Schüssen bei Paris
Ein Toter, vier Schwerverletzte - darunter ein Kind: Nach den Schüssen eines Autofahrers auf Passanten südwestlich von Paris ermittelt die Anti-Terror-Staatsanwaltschaft. Sie prüft auch, ob es einen rassistischen Hintergrund gibt.
Die beiden Kleinstädte Trappes und La Verrière südwestlich von Paris stehen unter Schock. Am späten Vormittag hatte ein Mann dort aus einem Auto auf Passanten geschossen. Innenminister Laurent Nuñez bestätigte, dass ein 39-jähriger Tatverdächtiger festgenommen wurde. Außerdem habe die französische Anti-Terror-Staatsanwaltschaft die Ermittlungen übernommen. Es handle sich um einen Terrorakt, sagte Nuñez.
Laut einer Pressemitteilung der Antiterror-Staatsanwaltschaft wird unter anderem wegen "Mordes in Verbindung mit einem terroristischen Vorhaben" ermittelt - in Zusammenhang mit der "tatsächlichen oder vermeintlichen Zugehörigkeit zu einer bestimmten (…) Ethnie, Nation oder Religion". Das könnte auf ein rassistisches Motiv hindeuten.
Was diese Einordnung betrifft, zeigt sich Aurore Bergé aber zurückhaltend. Sie ist als Ministerin zuständig für den Kampf gegen Diskriminierung und war am Nachmittag ebenfalls vor Ort. "Sollte sich der rassistische Charakter bestätigen, dann hoffe ich natürlich, dass die gesamte Nation sich hinter die Bewohner und die Opfer stellt", sagte sie. "Wir können in der französischen Republik keine auch noch so kleine rassistische oder diskriminierende Äußerung dulden. Wir wissen, dass Worte Gewalt nach sich ziehen können."
Bürgermeister: "Rassistisches Attentat"
Ali Rabeh, der Bürgermeister von Trappes, wählt deutlichere Worte. Er sprach von einem "rassistischen und wahrscheinlich islamfeindlichen Attentat". Laut Rabeh wurde ein Mann mit afrikanischen Wurzeln erschossen, einer der Verletzten stammt aus dem Maghreb. Bei der Festnahme seien eine Maschinenpistole sowie Tränengasgranaten sichergestellt worden, heißt es aus Polizeikreisen. Der Tatverdächtige sei vorbestraft, den Geheimdiensten bisher aber unbekannt.
In einem kurzen Pressestatement ging der Bürgermeister von der linken Partei Générations auch auf die zunehmend polarisierte Debatte in Frankreich ein.
                
                
                Uns muss allen klar sein: Auch die Sprache und der Diskurs, die das ideologische Rüstzeug für solche Täter liefern, sind kriminell – und das müssen wir so benennen. Wer als Minister, Abgeordneter oder Präsidentschaftskandidat erklärt, dass alle Probleme dieser Gesellschaft die Schuld von Arabern und Muslimen sind: dem muss klar sein, dass dieser Diskurs für Tote sorgt.
Ein weiteres Symptom für die Spaltung?
Die Schießerei in Trappes könnte die ohnehin angespannte Sicherheitslage in Frankreich weiter verschärfen. Nach den gewaltsamen Ausschreitungen in der vergangenen Woche ist für morgen ein neuer Protesttag angekündigt.
Laut Innenministerium werden rund um die Demonstrationen 70.000 Polizisten im Einsatz sein, darunter auch Spezialeinheiten der Polizei. In der ohnehin aufgeheizten politischen Atmosphäre könnte Trappes zu einem weiteren Symptom für die tiefe Spaltung der französischen Gesellschaft werden.
