title: Are California voters about to impose world's first 'tax on billionaires'?
content_c:
Are California voters about to impose world's first 'tax on billionaires'?
- Published
Few places on the planet have as many ultra-wealthy residents as California, a US state known for glamour, coastal mega-mansions and being home to many rich and famous.
Now voters are about to decide if the mega-rich among them - names that include media mogul Oprah Winfrey, Meta head Mark Zuckerberg, Skims cofounder and reality television star Kim Kardashian and filmmaker George Lucas - should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare.
Proposition 40 is aimed at levying a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California's billionaires.
There are a little more than 200 such individuals in the state - but that hasn't stopped the measure from dividing leaders and causing some of its ultra-wealthy residents to flee. One billionaire businessman says he's brought jobs to California, but the proposition made him feel "a little bit like I wasn't wanted".
- What are the US midterms? A simple guide 
  - Published6 October
But the vote is also offering regular everyday residents a voice on an issue that has riled politics for decades.
"I believe this is the first billionaire tax - meaning a wealth tax that is targeting a very extreme percentile of the wealth distribution," says Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He noted the measure's historic nature and how it could help even out California's wealth gap.
The state has the largest economy in the country - and boasts the fourth largest global economy, bigger than India and the whole of the UK. And it is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the globe. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps.
Those who back the measure have argued it helps ensure that the ultra-wealthy are contributing their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state's budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state's health-care system.
Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the charge for the initiative, says the measure is a "short-term solution" for massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.
"If we do nothing, we're going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare," she told the BBC.
While the ballot measure has many supporters - including some billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - it has faced fierce opposition from a variety of figures, from billionaires to the state's liberal governor.
Google co-founder Sergey Brin has given more than $100 million to a political nonprofit funding ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports, external.
California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.
A September poll, external from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided.
The statewide ballot measure would need to be approved by a majority of residents.
California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a "millionaires tax" - a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year.
While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now only exist in three European countries – Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs.
Niemietz believes wealth taxes are "more trouble than they are worth" because they cause administrative issues, suppress investment, lead to capital flight and, in the end, do not raise much revenue, she said.
In the case of Norway, a local news organisation found that an increase in the wealth tax led to more super wealthy people leaving the country in 2022, external than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland, external found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.
The California measure, if approved, would apply retroactively to those with a net worth of at least $1bn who resided in California as of 1 January 2026. At least six of the state's 200 plus billionaires have reportedly left California ahead of that deadline to avoid the tax.
They include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, venture capitalist Peter Thiel, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick and Hankey Group founder Don Hankey.
Hankey, a Los Angeles billionaire who has lived in California all his life, told Forbes he left for the state of Nevada as a result of the proposed wealth tax.
"I think we've created a lot of jobs in California. We have a few thousand people working for us and we have a profit sharing plan. And I have to leave the state," he added, saying the measure made him feel like he wasn't "wanted" in the state.
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg told the company's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California over the proposed tax. To prevent him from leaving the state - where the company is headquartered - Meta agreed to a new stock deal that gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn, even more shares in the company to make up for the billions he would lose if the measure passes in November. Estimates say he could owe as much as $12.5bn.
DoorDash cofounder Andy Fang, who has an estimated net worth of $1.6bn, has called the measure "stupid" and wrote on X that "proposals like this make it irresponsible for me not to plan leaving the state".
Meanwhile, businessman Tom Steyer, who ran an unsuccessful bid for California governor earlier this year, is one of the few billionaires who has said, external he would vote in favour of the tax. Steyer said that although he believes the way the measure is written is "problematic", it is necessary to protect vulnerable Californians.
Huang, too, has expressed support of paying the levy.
"I don't mind paying taxes. The more you make, the more taxes you pay. I'm okay with that," the Nvidia chief executive said in an interview with the BBC's news partner in the US, CBS. "I am the ultimate American Dream."
Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, a vocal champion against income inequality, has campaigned in support of Prop 40.
While at a Los Angeles rally, Sanders said billionaires "believe, like the monarchs of the 19th century, that they have a God-given right to rule".
"They have all the wealth; they got all the power, and who the hell do you think you are challenging them? Well, I think on Nov 3 they're going to learn a very powerful lesson".
Income inequality in the US is at some of its highest levels, external in over three decades, with the top 1% of households owning nearly 32% of all US wealth in the third quarter of 2025. It is also near historic highs in California.
Economic inequality is a concern among most Californians, with 72% believing that the gap between the rich and poor is widening and a similar share holding that state government should do more to reduce the gap, according to a statewide survey, external from the Public Policy Institute of California.
Trebbi says it is an "anti-elite, anti-system sentiment that is behind a policy" like Prop 40.
"This is really not about Prop 40," he says. It's about trying to "re-balance the scale a little bit".

And it is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the globe. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps.
Those who back the measure have argued it helps ensure that the ultra-wealthy are contributing their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state's budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state's health-care system.
Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the charge for the initiative, says the measure is a "short-term solution" for massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.
"If we do nothing, we're going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare," she told the BBC.
While the ballot measure has many supporters - including some billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - it has faced fierce opposition from a variety of figures, from billionaires to the state's liberal governor.
Google co-founder Sergey Brin has given more than $100 million to a political nonprofit funding ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports, external.
California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.
A September poll, external from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided.
The statewide ballot measure would need to be approved by a majority of residents.
California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a "millionaires tax" - a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year.
While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now only exist in three European countries – Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs.
Niemietz believes wealth taxes are "more trouble than they are worth" because they cause administrative issues, suppress investment, lead to capital flight and, in the end, do not raise much revenue, she said.
In the case of Norway, a local news organisation found that an increase in the wealth tax led to more super wealthy people leaving the country in 2022, external than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland, external found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.
The California measure, if approved, would apply retroactively to those with a net worth of at least $1bn who resided in California as of 1 January 2026. At least six of the state's 200 plus billionaires have reportedly left California ahead of that deadline to avoid the tax.
They include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, venture capitalist Peter Thiel, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick and Hankey Group founder Don Hankey.
Hankey, a Los Angeles billionaire who has lived in California all his life, told Forbes he left for the state of Nevada as a result of the proposed wealth tax.
"I think we've created a lot of jobs in California. We have a few thousand people working for us and we have a profit sharing plan. And I have to leave the state," he added, saying the measure made him feel like he wasn't "wanted" in the state.
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg told the company's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California over the proposed tax. To prevent him from leaving the state - where the company is headquartered - Meta agreed to a new stock deal that gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn, even more shares in the company to make up for the billions he would lose if the measure passes in November. Estimates say he could owe as much as $12.5bn.
DoorDash cofounder Andy Fang, who has an estimated net worth of $1.6bn, has called the measure "stupid" and wrote on X that "proposals like this make it irresponsible for me not to plan leaving the state".
Meanwhile, businessman Tom Steyer, who ran an unsuccessful bid for California governor earlier this year, is one of the few billionaires who has said, external he would vote in favour of the tax. Steyer said that although he believes the way the measure is written is "problematic", it is necessary to protect vulnerable Californians.
Huang, too, has expressed support of paying the levy.
"I don't mind paying taxes. The more you make, the more taxes you pay. I'm okay with that," the Nvidia chief executive said in an interview with the BBC's news partner in the US, CBS. "I am the ultimate American Dream."
Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, a vocal champion against income inequality, has campaigned in support of Prop 40.
While at a Los Angeles rally, Sanders said billionaires "believe, like the monarchs of the 19th century, that they have a God-given right to rule".
"They have all the wealth; they got all the power, and who the hell do you think you are challenging them? Well, I think on Nov 3 they're going to learn a very powerful lesson".
Income inequality in the US is at some of its highest levels, external in over three decades, with the top 1% of households owning nearly 32% of all US wealth in the third quarter of 2025. It is also near historic highs in California.
Economic inequality is a concern among most Californians, with 72% believing that the gap between the rich and poor is widening and a similar share holding that state government should do more to reduce the gap, according to a statewide survey, external from the Public Policy Institute of California.
Trebbi says it is an "anti-elite, anti-system sentiment that is behind a policy" like Prop 40.
"This is really not about Prop 40," he says. It's about trying to "re-balance the scale a little bit".

title: John Healey pledges to use budget to harness power of AI to bolster Britain’s security
content_c:
John Healey has pledged to use Wednesday’s budget to harness the power of artificial intelligence to bolster Britain’s security and prosperity against the risks in the accelerating global technology arms race.
As he prepares for his debut budget, the chancellor said that Andy Burnham’s government would commit hundreds of millions of pounds to develop a “distinctively British” approach to AI that would capitalise on the benefits of the frontier technology.
At a fork in the road as AI developments pose both existential threats and transformative economic potential, Healey said he would be making the biggest ever investment to guard against cyber risks and the disruptive potential of the technology.
As part of the measures in his tax and spending statement, he promised fresh investment for Britain’s AI Security Institute and other critical institutions, alongside allocating public money to support the use of the technology for good.
“AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school and every aspect of our economy can benefit,” Healey said.
“I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI – one that doesn’t leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country.”
Three months into Burnham’s premiership, Healey is poised to deliver a budget against an increasingly volatile backdrop as the war in the Middle East sends shock waves through the global economy, putting pressure on public finances and reigniting the cost of living crisis.
The chancellor has vowed to use his first budget to provide households and businesses with “breathing space” as the global surge in energy costs triggered by the war hits millions of families this winter. On Friday, the latest tensions in the Gulf sent the oil price to its highest level for six months, rising above $117 a barrel at one point.
However he will also use the opportunity afforded by the critical speech to the Commons to flesh out Burnham’s policy priorities for government after he replaced Keir Starmer this summer, and to spell out a vision for Britain amid the increasingly turbulent global economic outlook.
Aiming to harness the opportunities of AI to raise living standards, back UK businesses and support economic growth, the chancellor said he wanted to seize the opportunities of the technology as a central plank of Labour’s plan for growth.
It comes after official figures show AI investment has helped the UK outperform gloomy economic forecasts as the Iran war pushes up inflation and drags down business confidence, powering the country to the strongest growth performance in the G7 in the first half of this year.
However, there are growing fears over the security of the nation and critical industries as the technology opens up the danger of cyber-attacks, IT systems turning rogue and devastating job losses as companies invest in machines rather than humans.
It comes as websites around the globe went dark this week after a serious vulnerability was found in a computer language used to build much of the world wide web, in a development made possible by rapid AI advances. It also emerged this week that Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs as part of cost-saving plans identified by bosses as the rollout of AI across the bank helps it make efficiency gains.
Healey said he wanted to use his budget to protect against risks while also nurturing homegrown businesses and talent, in order to cut Britain’s dependency on other countries that were also making strides in AI technology.
New investments would be made in AI chip design capability in Edinburgh, alongside a new AI Centre of Excellence in Manchester that it said would enable the UK to harness the technology’s benefits.
The government would also spend £10m a year to lead the UK’s work on understanding how AI will reshape jobs and industry, aiming to address concerns about potential job disruption.
As part of the plan the Treasury said it would back up to £300m in public-private investment in a new AI Biosecurity Lab, designed to serve as a world-leading institution bringing together scientific expertise to protect people from emerging biological threats.
It comes after the defence secretary, Wes Streeting, warned on Thursday that UK households should make preparations against the mounting risks from weather, cyber or other serious emergencies.
The advice to stock up on supplies to last 72 hours, in a campaign called Be Ready, comes as Silicon Valley bosses sound the alarm over the increasingly existential threats AI could pose, and amid growing official concern over the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.
Dan Jarvis, the security minister, said: “I’m proud the UK has repeatedly been at the forefront of global efforts to use AI for the benefit of humankind.
“Today’s investment will help the UK seize the opportunities AI presents to strengthen our national security, while staying one step ahead of those who seek to use AI to do us harm.”

title: Germany news: Wadephul says 'threat of famine' due to ongoing wars
content_c:
Germany news: Wadephul says 'threat of famine' due to ongoing wars
Published October 23, 2026last updated October 23, 2026
What you need to know
These updates have been closed. Thank you for joining us.
Below, you can review what Germany was talking about on Friday, 23 October, 2026. .
- German Foreign Minister Wadephul met counterparts in Istanbul, Turkey
- Bavarian CSU kicks off two-day party conference in Munich
- Pakistani president expected in Berlin
- Survey: lack of support for left-wing coalition in Berlin's Senate
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
Wadephul offers Iran talks with Germany, UK, France
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said the conflicts threatening free shipping, such as the Iran-backed Houthi rebels firing at vessels in the Red Sea, could not be solved militarily.
Wadephul is attending a summit in Istanbul, joined by foreign ministers from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt, France and the UK.
Commenting on the ongoing crises in the Red Sea and off the coast of Ukraine, the German minister said his country was willing to negotiate with Iran, together with France and the UK.
The three European countries were among the signatories of the 2015 JCPOA deal with Iran which was torn up by Donald Trump during his first term in office.
Wadephul also urged Russia to make a deal to secure shipping in the Black Sea.
Bayern coach Kompany brought to hospital
Vincent Kompany, the coach of the Bundesliga's Bayern Munich, was hospitalized on Friday, according to team officials.
"Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during a training session for Bayern’s reserve team," the club said. "The head coach of the professional squad had been observing the second team's session."
"Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training and match-related operations."
Currently leading the Bundesliga, Bayern drew 2-2 in a Champions League match against UK's Arsenal this week.
“Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority," said Max Eberl, Bayern's Board Member for Sport.
"Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and he will be given as much time as he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery."
Hacked AfD emails put spotlight on Weidel over illegal donations
After hackers targeted Germany's far-right AfD party and published hundreds of thousands of internal emails online this week, German magazine Der Spiegel published a report highlighting a 2017 exchange regarding illegal donations from Switzerland.
German parties are legally forbidden from receiving donations from non-EU countries.
The scandal already prompted a formal probe in 2018, which ended with authorities imposing fines that amounted to over half a million euros (around $565,000). German prosecutors also opened a formal probe into the party's prominent co-leader, Alice Weidel. The probe was closed in 2021 due to insufficient evidence.
Weidel has claimed that she only learned of the "unsolicited" donations in September 2017 and decided to return the money due to "legal concerns."
But the recently leaked emails indicate Weidel told a regional party treasurer to be on the lookout for "possible incoming donations" in July 2017, just days before the money started coming in. In August, the treasurer referred to a "benefactor from Switzerland" who supports Weidel with thousands of Swiss francs per week.
When contacted by the AFP news agency on Friday, Weidel's spokesperson said the AfD leader was not revising "any of her statements regarding the matter."
"Ms. Weidel neither expected specific amounts nor was she certain that individual persons would actually donate" and did not expect the payments from Switzerland, her press representative said.
WATCH — AfD scrambling after data breach
Germany’s far-right AfD is investigating the extent of the damage from a massive data breach. Hackers copied hundreds of thousands of emails and sensitive documents.
The data has been published online, and the first excerpts are slowly being made public. The AfD has reported the matter to the relevant authorities and appealed to the media not to publish "stolen" data.
Merz to travel to Asia next week
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will travel to Japan, Singapore and South Korea next week for meetings on economic and security policy, according to deputy government spokesman Steffen Meyer.
"We share with all three countries a commitment to open, rules-based trade and a desire to strengthen economic resilience and security, particularly with regard to global supply chains," said Meyer during a Friday press conference.
Merz is scheduled to depart Berlin on Monday and return Friday. He will be accompanied by a German business delegation.
All three countries possess "great innovative power," said Meyer, "that is why we want to deepen collaboration on future-relevant topics such a AI."
Merz will begin his trip by visiting Singapore on Tuesday, where he will meet the prime minister and president before delivering a speech.
On Wednesday, he will travel to Tokyo to meet the prime minister and take part in a German-Japanese economic summit.
Merz will end his trip in South Korea where he will meet with the president before kicking off the 19th annual Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business (APK), in Seoul.
Wadephul warns shipping disruptions could lead to famine
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has warned that continuing disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea could potentially lead to famine in the global south.
"We're all feeling the effects of the attacks on shipping lanes, whether at the gas station or in the supermarket," he said ahead of a meeting with fellow foreign ministers in Istanbul on Friday. "But elsewhere, there is a threat of famine when fertilizers don't arrive in the places where they are essential for basic production."
Wadephul was referring not only to the Iranian closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi threats to the Bab al-Mandab strait, but also to Russian attacks on shipping in the Black Sea as part of Moscow's ongoing war against Ukraine, one of the world's leading producers of wheat.
"This effects the poorest people in the world whose basic provisions are especially dependent on wheat, as well as our partners such as Turkey, the biggest wheat processing country in the world," he said.
"Together, we want to send a signal: we will not accept Iran and the Houthi militias [in Yemen] holding global trade hostage," Wadephul continued.
"The indiscriminatory attacks on free shipping and on neighboring countries must stop. For people across the region who are suffering from hunger, who no longer feel safe in their own homes, the continuing insecurity is not acceptable."
Prosecutors say Federal Court of Justice executed arrest warrant for suspected Russian spy
German Federal Prosecutors said Friday that a judge from the Federal Court of Justice in Karlsruhe had ordered the detention of a Ukrainian man arrested by police in the eastern state of Brandenburg on Thursday.
The man is accused of spying on German and NATO military installations in the country on behalf of Russian intelligence services.
Investigators say he sought to collect information on the production of armored vehicles, explosives and munitions. Moreover, he collected information on military personnel and facilities tasked with protecting NATO's eastern flank.
President of Pakistan visits Berlin
The President of Pakistan, Asif Ali Zardari, was expected to be received with military honors in Berlin on Friday, at the start of a two-day visit to mark the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Germany.
The Pakistani foreign ministry said in a statement that Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as with senior business leaders.
The statement placed a particular focus on "economic and trade cooperation" and said the visit "reflects the deep commitment of both countries to the further strengthening the partnership."
Like President Steinmeier in Germany, President Zardari is Pakistan's official head of state, a largely ceremonial role. Real political power in Pakistan lies theoretically with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and currently de facto with the influential head of the armed forces, Field Marshall Asim Munir.
Partly for that reason, Berlin's Tagesspiegel newspaper expressed skepticism over Zardari's visit, describing him as a "powerless president," highlighting past corruption scandals, criticizing the treatment of German media outlets in Pakistan and questioning why Germany was investing political capital in deeper relations with the Islamic Republic.
The newspaper opined that Islamabad's mediatory role in the Middle East isn't as influential as it seems and suggested that Pakistan's neighbor and rival India was a significantly more important trading partner for both Germany and the European Union.
It did say acknowledge that "Germany cannot ignore Pakistan" as a nuclear power on the frontline of climate change and as a country with a rapidly growing population, but ultimately concluded that Zardari's visit was more "FOMO" (fear of missing out) than real diplomatic "strategy."
Germany: Bavarian CSU kicks off party conference in Munich
The Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), begins its two-day party conference in Munich on Friday.
Together, the CDU and CSU form Germany's center-right "Union" and, despite plunging ratings for Merz and the CDU nationally, backing for the CSU in Bavaria remains relatively strong, with two recent polls putting support at between 36% and 37%.
Nevertheless, there is still concern in Munich that the Union's struggles in the coalition government in Berlin and growing support for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), including in Bavaria, could threaten the CSU's status as a "big tent party" or Volkspartei.
Chancellor Merz will address delegates on Saturday but few in Munich are hopeful of a positive change of course. And all the while, CSU leader and Bavarian State Premier Markus Söder remains waiting in the wings as a potential challenger to Merz at the national level.
The charismatic, self-confident 59-year-old dominates Bavarian politics and, according to sources who spoke to the DPA news agency, would be ready to step up if called upon.
But a leadership challenge is not expected to be a serious proposition until April 2027 when another senior Union figure and potential chancellor candidate, Hendrik Wüst (CDU), runs in local elections in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW), where he is currently serving as state premier.
For this weekend, however, the conservatives' focus is on Bavaria.
Wadephul in Istanbul for 'R4+E3' foreign ministers summit
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul (CDU) was expected in Istanbul, Turkey, on Friday ahead of a meeting with his Turkish, Saudi Arabian, Pakistani, Egyptian, French and British counterparts.
The foreign ministers are set to discuss a range of geopolitical issues including, according to a spokesperson for the Turkish foreign ministry, "the Palestine question, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments in Yemen and the search for an end to the war in Ukraine."
For the seven ministers, the event marks a first such meeting in the so-called "R4+E3" format. The E3, consisting of Germany, France and the United Kingdom, was established in the early 2000s amid nuclear negotiations with Iran, while Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt formed the R4 earlier this year to coordinate a joint regional response to the US-Israeli war on Iran.
"At our first meeting in this format, we Europeans and the four regional powers want to discuss together how we can inject fresh impetus into the conflicts in the Strait of Hormuz, around [the] Bab al-Mandab [strait] and in the Black Sea," said Wadephul ahead of his departure.
"We can only deal with these massive challenges if we work together beyond established formats," he continued, adding that "these gridlocked conflicts" which have "significant economic and security consequences for our countries" have also created a fresh "desire to look for new solutions."
Welcome to our coverage
Guten Morgen! Welcome to DW's coverage of what Germany is talking about on Friday, 23 October.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is set to meet with European and Middle Eastern counterparts in Turkey for discussions on a series of regional geopolitical crises including developments in the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories and Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.
Back in Germany, the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), is launching its two-day party conference in Munich.
In Berlin, a new survey suggests a lack of support for a potential left-wing Senate coalition between the Left Party, the Social Democrats (SPD) and the Greens.
And while Foreign Minister Wadehul meets the Pakistani foreign minister in Istanbul, Pakistan's president, Ali Zardari, is expected to be welcomed to Berlin.
description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is joining counterparts in Turkey for discussions on a range of interlinked geopolitical crises. Back in Germany, the Bavarian CSU party begins its two-day conference in Munich.

"This effects the poorest people in the world whose basic provisions are especially dependent on wheat, as well as our partners such as Turkey, the biggest wheat processing country in the world," he said.
"Together, we want to send a signal: we will not accept Iran and the Houthi militias [in Yemen] holding global trade hostage," Wadephul continued.
"The indiscriminatory attacks on free shipping and on neighboring countries must stop. For people across the region who are suffering from hunger, who no longer feel safe in their own homes, the continuing insecurity is not acceptable."
Prosecutors say Federal Court of Justice executed arrest warrant for suspected Russian spy
German Federal Prosecutors said Friday that a judge from the Federal Court of Justice in Karlsruhe had ordered the detention of a Ukrainian man arrested by police in the eastern state of Brandenburg on Thursday.
The man is accused of spying on German and NATO military installations in the country on behalf of Russian intelligence services.
Investigators say he sought to collect information on the production of armored vehicles, explosives and munitions. Moreover, he collected information on military personnel and facilities tasked with protecting NATO's eastern flank.
President of Pakistan visits Berlin
The President of Pakistan, Asif Ali Zardari, was expected to be received with military honors in Berlin on Friday, at the start of a two-day visit to mark the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Germany.
The Pakistani foreign ministry said in a statement that Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as with senior business leaders.
The statement placed a particular focus on "economic and trade cooperation" and said the visit "reflects the deep commitment of both countries to the further strengthening the partnership."
Like President Steinmeier in Germany, President Zardari is Pakistan's official head of state, a largely ceremonial role. Real political power in Pakistan lies theoretically with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and currently de facto with the influential head of the armed forces, Field Marshall Asim Munir.
Partly for that reason, Berlin's Tagesspiegel newspaper expressed skepticism over Zardari's visit, describing him as a "powerless president," highlighting past corruption scandals, criticizing the treatment of German media outlets in Pakistan and questioning why Germany was investing political capital in deeper relations with the Islamic Republic.
The newspaper opined that Islamabad's mediatory role in the Middle East isn't as influential as it seems and suggested that Pakistan's neighbor and rival India was a significantly more important trading partner for both Germany and the European Union.
It did say acknowledge that "Germany cannot ignore Pakistan" as a nuclear power on the frontline of climate change and as a country with a rapidly growing population, but ultimately concluded that Zardari's visit was more "FOMO" (fear of missing out) than real diplomatic "strategy."
Germany: Bavarian CSU kicks off party conference in Munich
The Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), begins its two-day party conference in Munich on Friday.
Together, the CDU and CSU form Germany's center-right "Union" and, despite plunging ratings for Merz and the CDU nationally, backing for the CSU in Bavaria remains relatively strong, with two recent polls putting support at between 36% and 37%.
Nevertheless, there is still concern in Munich that the Union's struggles in the coalition government in Berlin and growing support for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), including in Bavaria, could threaten the CSU's status as a "big tent party" or Volkspartei.
Chancellor Merz will address delegates on Saturday but few in Munich are hopeful of a positive change of course. And all the while, CSU leader and Bavarian State Premier Markus Söder remains waiting in the wings as a potential challenger to Merz at the national level.
The charismatic, self-confident 59-year-old dominates Bavarian politics and, according to sources who spoke to the DPA news agency, would be ready to step up if called upon.
But a leadership challenge is not expected to be a serious proposition until April 2027 when another senior Union figure and potential chancellor candidate, Hendrik Wüst (CDU), runs in local elections in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW), where he is currently serving as state premier.
For this weekend, however, the conservatives' focus is on Bavaria.
Wadephul in Istanbul for 'R4+E3' foreign ministers summit
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul (CDU) was expected in Istanbul, Turkey, on Friday ahead of a meeting with his Turkish, Saudi Arabian, Pakistani, Egyptian, French and British counterparts.
The foreign ministers are set to discuss a range of geopolitical issues including, according to a spokesperson for the Turkish foreign ministry, "the Palestine question, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments in Yemen and the search for an end to the war in Ukraine."
For the seven ministers, the event marks a first such meeting in the so-called "R4+E3" format. The E3, consisting of Germany, France and the United Kingdom, was established in the early 2000s amid nuclear negotiations with Iran, while Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt formed the R4 earlier this year to coordinate a joint regional response to the US-Israeli war on Iran.
"At our first meeting in this format, we Europeans and the four regional powers want to discuss together how we can inject fresh impetus into the conflicts in the Strait of Hormuz, around [the] Bab al-Mandab [strait] and in the Black Sea," said Wadephul ahead of his departure.
"We can only deal with these massive challenges if we work together beyond established formats," he continued, adding that "these gridlocked conflicts" which have "significant economic and security consequences for our countries" have also created a fresh "desire to look for new solutions."
Welcome to our coverage
Guten Morgen! Welcome to DW's coverage of what Germany is talking about on Friday, 23 October.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is set to meet with European and Middle Eastern counterparts in Turkey for discussions on a series of regional geopolitical crises including developments in the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories and Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.
Back in Germany, the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), is launching its two-day party conference in Munich.
In Berlin, a new survey suggests a lack of support for a potential left-wing Senate coalition between the Left Party, the Social Democrats (SPD) and the Greens.
And while Foreign Minister Wadehul meets the Pakistani foreign minister in Istanbul, Pakistan's president, Ali Zardari, is expected to be welcomed to Berlin.

title: Midterms in Alaska: US-Justizministerium reicht Klage wegen doppeltem Dan Sullivan ein
content_c:
Parlamentswahl in Alaska US-Justizministerium reicht Klage wegen Dan Sullivan ein, um Niederlage von Dan Sullivan zu verhindern
Die US-Regierung von Donald Trump hat einen drastischen Eingriff in die Parlamentswahlen in Alaska angekündigt. Wegen einer möglichen Verwechslungsgefahr zwischen den beiden republikanischen Kandidaten Dan S. Sullivan und Dan J. Sullivan für den dortigen Senatssitz reichte das Justizministerium eine Klage gegen den Bundesstaat ein.
Im Falle einer Niederlage des derzeitigen Senators Dan S. Sullivan fordert das US-Justizministerium, dass erst eine Untersuchung feststellen muss, ob er ohne seinen nahezu namensgleichen Kontrahenten auf dem Wahlzettel mehr Stimmen erhalten hätte. Dadurch solle die »Integrität der Senatswahl 2026 in Alaska« geschützt werden.
Im umkämpften Bundesstaat Alaska konkurrieren mehrere Politiker um einen Senatsposten: Neben dem republikanischen Amtsinhaber Dan S. Sullivan und der Demokratin Mary Peltola tritt auch der ebenfalls republikanische Herausforderer Dan J. Sullivan an. Bei den US-Kongresswahlen am 3. November werden alle 435 Sitze im Repräsentantenhaus und 35 der 100 Senatsposten neu gewählt.
Das Justizministerium wirft dem unbekannten Außenseiter vor: »Der einzige Zweck seiner Kandidatur ist es, Peltolas Wahlkampf zu fördern, indem die Zahl der Stimmen für Senator Sullivan reduziert wird.« So habe sich der Herausforderer erst kurz vor der Erklärung seiner Kandidatur den Republikanern angeschlossen. Zudem habe er denselben Namen wie der Amtsinhaber beantragt, obwohl er diesen »zuvor nie« in dieser Kurzform verwendet habe.
US-Präsident Donald Trump bestätigte die Vorgänge. Er selbst habe das Justizministerium zu diesem Schritt aufgefordert. Im Gespräch mit Journalisten sagte er, Dan J. Sullivan sei Teil einer Strategie der Demokraten, um eine Wiederwahl des republikanischen Amtsinhabers zu verhindern.
Es ist nicht das erste Mal, dass eine mögliche Verwechslungsgefahr Gegenstand einer juristischen Auseinandersetzung war. Bereits zuvor hatte die Wahlleiterin Alaskas versucht, den Herausforderer Sullivan vom Stimmzettel zu streichen. Der Oberste Gerichtshof des Bundesstaates entschied allerdings, dass er rechtmäßig antreten dürfe.
Der derzeitige Senator Dan S. Sullivan vertritt den Bundesstaat seit 2015 in Washington. Über Dan J. Sullivan ist nur wenig zu erfahren. Anders als die anderen Kandidaten hat der 69-Jährige keine Wahlkampfauftritte absolviert.
description: Kandidiert Dan J. Sullivan nur, um Dan S. Sullivan die Stimmen zu stehlen? Davon geht offenbar die US-Regierung aus. Um das zu verhindern, hat das Justizministerium nun rechtliche Schritte eingeleitet.

title: Ein Toter und Verletzte: Innenminister spricht von Terror-Tat bei Paris
content_c:
Toter und Verletzte nach Schüssen Innenminister spricht von Terror-Tat bei Paris
Aus einem Auto heraus hat ein Mann in mehreren Vororten von Paris Schüsse abgefeuert. Ein Mensch wurde getötet, es gibt mehrere Schwerverletzte. Frankreichs Innenminister Nuñez spricht von einer "terroristischen Tat".
In der Region Paris hat ein Mann aus einem Auto heraus auf offener Straße das Feuer eröffnet und mindestens einen Menschen getötet. Zudem gebe es mindestens vier Verletzte, teilte die französische Nationalpolizei mit. Der 39-jährige Tatverdächtige sei festgenommen worden. Die französische Anti-Terror-Staatsanwaltschaft teilte mit, sie habe eine Untersuchung eingeleitet.
Innenminister Laurent Nuñez sprach von einer "terroristischen Tat". Zwar liefen die Ermittlungen noch, sagte er vor Journalistinnen und Journalisten. "Aber es handelt sich eindeutig um ein terroristisches Verbrechen." Die Motive müssten noch abschließend geklärt werden. Unter Berufung auf den zuständigen Staatsanwalt führte Nuñez aus, dass die Hintergründe rassistischer Natur sein könnten. Weitere Informationen gab es zunächst nicht.
Schüsse an drei verschiedenen Orten
Laut dem Minister schoss der Verdächtige mit einer automatischen Waffe. Die vier Verletzten seien schwer verletzt. Unter ihnen ist französischen Medien zufolge ein zwölfjähriges Kind. Der Verdächtige habe an drei verschiedenen Orten aus dem Wagen heraus geschossen. Der Vorfall ereignete sich im Département Yvelines, das im westlichen Teil der Pariser Großraumregion liegt.
Zunächst fielen Schüsse in der Gemeinde Trappes, dann fuhr der Mann den Angaben nach weiter in die angrenzende kleine Gemeinde La Verrière. Der Bürgermeister von Trappes, Ali Rabeh, sagte dem Sender BFMTV, der Mann habe offensichtlich wahllos geschossen und ein "Blutbad" anrichten wollen. Das Todesopfer sei "afrikanischer Herkunft", ein Verletzter in Lebensgefahr sei zudem "maghrebinischer Herkunft".
Anti-Terror-Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt
Die französische Anti-Terror-Staatsanwaltschaft teilte mit, sie habe ein Ermittlungsverfahren wegen "Mordes im Zusammenhang mit einer terroristischen Vereinigung" eingeleitet. Die Tat sei zudem "aufgrund der tatsächlichen oder vermeintlichen Zugehörigkeit zu einer angeblichen Rasse, Ethnie, Nation oder bestimmten Religion begangen" worden.
Die Ermittlungen betreffen außerdem den Tatbestand des "Besitzes einer Waffe der Kategorie A", zu der insbesondere automatische Waffen gehören, die Salven abgeben, sowie der "Beteiligung an einer terroristischen kriminellen Vereinigung mit dem Ziel der Vorbereitung von Verbrechen gegen Menschen".
"Sehr ernste Vorfälle"
Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu schrieb auf der Plattform X, Sicherheits- und Justizbehörden seien in vollem Einsatz. Es handele sich um "sehr ernste Vorfälle". Alle Ressourcen der Sicherheitskräfte und der Justiz seien in vollem Umfang mobilisiert.
Angesichts von Protesten und Unruhen ist die Sicherheitslage in Frankreich derzeit angespannt. Am Wochenende war es am Rande von Demonstrationen gegen hohe Lebenshaltungskosten und Missstände im Bildungssystem zu massiven Ausschreitungen gekommen. Als Reaktion darauf wurden in mehreren Großstädten nächtliche Ausgangssperren verhängt.

title: Тисяча гривень за поїздку або мототаксі: як у Києві виживають під час транспортного колапсу — відео
content_c:
Тисяча гривень за поїздку або мототаксі: як у Києві виживають під час транспортного колапсу — відео
Як кияни долають Дніпро під час повітряних тривог: стрибок цін на таксі, зупинка червоної гілки метро, автобуси та експеримент із мототаксі.
Знеструмлення, завивання сирен та паралізована робота метро. А ще — зупинені просто під час руху тролейбуси і трамваї. І це фактично щоразу, коли Кремль цілить у нашу критичну інфраструктуру. Для киян ранки вже перетворилися на квест: як дістатися на роботу, особливо коли вона на іншому березі Дніпра? Над головою постійно гудуть російські дрони, наземний громадський транспорт переповнений, а цінник на таксі під час тривоги множиться у кілька разів.
То скільки сил, часу і грошей вартує дорога на роботу під виття сирен? І як можливо це змінити, йдеться у матеріалі кореспондентки ТСН ІриниКондрачук.
Ранковий квест: ціни на таксі та зупинка червоної гілки
Години в черзі, штурм переповнених автобусів, коли над головою летять дрони, та космічні ціни на таксі. Як перетнути Дніпро у годину пік? ТСН провела експеримент і з’ясувала, чи намагається влада розв’язати проблему транспортного колапсу.
Між лівим берегом (від станції метро «Дарниця») і правим (до офісу 1+1) — відстань у 11 кілометрів дороги. Ще до початку повітряної тривоги моніторинг додатків виклику авто показує: 449 гривень за стандартний тариф, комфорт — понад 500 гривень, а швидкий пошук сягає майже 600 гривень.
На годиннику пів на восьму ранку. ТСН вирушає в розвідку з правого на лівий берег. При перетині Дніпра у зворотньому напрямку вже помітно щільний трафік на мосту та заповнені вагони метро.
Але рівно о 8:00 ранку, коли більшість людей добирається на роботу, лунає сирена про небезпеку. У Києві оголошують повітряну тривогу через загрозу дронової атаки. Це означає, що червона гілка метрополітену зупиняється, адже потяги курсують над землею. Усі, хто був у підземці, опиняються на вулиці.
Чому злітають тарифи на таксі та що пропонує реформа
У додатках таксі ціни миттєво летять угору. У службах виклику авто пояснюють: підвищення може сягати до трьох з половиною разів, і це робиться для того, щоб мотивувати водіїв виїхати на виклики у райони з підвищеним попитом.
Олена Орлова, представниця українського сервісу виклику таксі: «Головна мета даного механізму в нашому випадку взагалі — збалансувати ринок сервісу виклику авто і зробити так, щоб максимальна кількість водіїв потрапила в ті райони, де найбільш підвищений попит».
Вплинути на це ціноутворення наразі не може ніхто, адже ринок таксі залишається неврегульованим.
Андрій Антонюк, директор ГО «Українська таксомоторна асоціація»: «Ринок на 99% є нелегальним. Люди працюють в основному не як суб’єкти підприємництва, не платять податки. І цій проблемі вже десятиріччя».
В уряді проблему визнають та оцінюють у конкретних цифрах.
Сергій Деркач, перший заступник міністра інфраструктури: «Державний бюджет недоотримує в рік близько 5 мільярдів гривень. Це виключно з тих податків, які мали б платитися в бюджет саме водіями таксі на сьогодні. Це немаленька сума, яку точно можна було витратити якраз на користь транспортної сфери, як мінімум».
Наразі Кабмін разом із народними депутатами готує реформу таксі. Насамперед планують з’ясувати точну кількість водіїв у країні через запровадження електронної реєстрації, яка дозволить отримати статус водія за добу. Пасажири матимуть доступ до інформації про керманича. Також передбачено податок для цифрових платформ служб таксі й доставок у розмірі 5,5% та їхню відповідальність за наявність у водіїв техогляду й страховки. відповідний законопроект вже проходить останні кола погодження і незабаром потрапить до парламенту.
Щодо диктування тарифів під час тривог: уряд не планує регулювати ціни зверху, посилаючись на європейський досвід, де це належить до компетенції місцевої влади. Однак у Департаменті транспортної інфраструктури КМДА від регулювання таксі відхрещуються, зазначаючи у відповіді, що питання будь-якого регулювання діяльності служб таксі не належить до їхньої компетенції.
Альтернативні маршрути, автобуси та поради експертів
Щоб полегшити ситуацію на дорогах, місто змінило схеми руху окремих маршрутів громадського транспорту. Зупинену червону гілку метро дублюють автобуси, але їх катастрофічно бракує, а чекати доводиться не менше 40 хвилин.
Водії та пасажири автобусів: «Автобус не поїде, поки не закриються двері! Ви бачите, що ви не влазите? Куди ви лізете?!»
Проблема полягає не лише в кількості автобусів, а й у самому довгому маршруті («Метро Лісова» — «Палац Спорту»), який збирає затори в центрі міста.
Наталія Волик, фахівчиня з транспортної політики ГО «Екодія»: «Чому він їде таким складним маршрутом і аж до центру міста? Він збирає на собі частину заторів і виходить, що не виконує головну функцію — сполучити по червоній гілці людей із правим берегом».
Експертка наголошує, що Києву передусім потрібні спрощені маршрути та єдиний квиток на увесь громадський транспорт (включаючи метро), щоб пасажири у разі зупинки підземки не сплачували двічі. Серед інших швидких рішень — збільшення смуг для громадського транспорту та розбудова велоінфраструктури.
Народна самоорганізація: від міської електрички до мототаксі
Поки системні рішення перебувають на стадії обговорень, кияни рятуються самотужки.
Містяни про альтернативні шляхи: «Коли я бачу, що зранку тривога, то я вже зразу йду на електричку».
Одні моніторять рух міської електрички від «Укрзалізниці», інші беруть у прокат самокати, пересідають на велосипеди, шукають попутки у Telegram-каналах або користуються автостопом — хтось везе безкоштовно «за шоколадку», хтось бере символічні 50–100 гривень.
Трапляються і нестандартні рішення, наприклад, мототаксі з лівого на правий берег. Водій мототаксі Павло розповідає, що об’їжджає затори за лічені хвилини.
Павло, водій мототаксі: «Є дешеві варіанти, коли з одного берега перекинути на інший — 200 гривень. Це стандартна ціна, вона не змінюється від того, тепло чи холодно на вулиці, є затори чи немає».
У Павла вже пів сотні постійних клієнтів після допису в соцмережі Threads. Він каже, що не єдиний, хто надає такі послуги у столиці. Для поїздок пропонується шолом, одноразова шапочка, а за температури нижче +10°C — зимові рукавиці.
Журналістка ТСН особисто випробувала цей спосіб пересування, щоб дістатися з лівого берега на Подол. Завдяки маневреності мотоцикл легко долав затори та доїхав до фінішу швидше за знімальну групу на авто.
Попри альтернативні варіанти, мототаксі залишається рішенням не для кожного, а кияни продовжують щоранку долати транспортні виклики під час обстрілів та тривог.

description: Як кияни долають Дніпро під час повітряних тривог: стрибок цін на таксі, зупинка червоної гілки метро, автобуси та експеримент із мототаксі.
content:
Тисяча гривень за поїздку або мототаксі: як у Києві виживають під час транспортного колапсу — відео
Як кияни долають Дніпро під час повітряних тривог: стрибок цін на таксі, зупинка червоної гілки метро, автобуси та експеримент із мототаксі.
Знеструмлення, завивання сирен та паралізована робота метро. А ще — зупинені просто під час руху тролейбуси і трамваї. І це фактично щоразу, коли Кремль цілить у нашу критичну інфраструктуру. Для киян ранки вже перетворилися на квест: як дістатися на роботу, особливо коли вона на іншому березі Дніпра? Над головою постійно гудуть російські дрони, наземний громадський транспорт переповнений, а цінник на таксі під час тривоги множиться у кілька разів.
То скільки сил, часу і грошей вартує дорога на роботу під виття сирен? І як можливо це змінити, йдеться у матеріалі кореспондентки ТСН ІриниКондрачук.
Ранковий квест: ціни на таксі та зупинка червоної гілки
Години в черзі, штурм переповнених автобусів, коли над головою летять дрони, та космічні ціни на таксі. Як перетнути Дніпро у годину пік? ТСН провела експеримент і з’ясувала, чи намагається влада розв’язати проблему транспортного колапсу.
Між лівим берегом (від станції метро «Дарниця») і правим (до офісу 1+1) — відстань у 11 кілометрів дороги. Ще до початку повітряної тривоги моніторинг додатків виклику авто показує: 449 гривень за стандартний тариф, комфорт — понад 500 гривень, а швидкий пошук сягає майже 600 гривень.
На годиннику пів на восьму ранку. ТСН вирушає в розвідку з правого на лівий берег. При перетині Дніпра у зворотньому напрямку вже помітно щільний трафік на мосту та заповнені вагони метро.
Але рівно о 8:00 ранку, коли більшість людей добирається на роботу, лунає сирена про небезпеку. У Києві оголошують повітряну тривогу через загрозу дронової атаки. Це означає, що червона гілка метрополітену зупиняється, адже потяги курсують над землею. Усі, хто був у підземці, опиняються на вулиці.
Чому злітають тарифи на таксі та що пропонує реформа
У додатках таксі ціни миттєво летять угору. У службах виклику авто пояснюють: підвищення може сягати до трьох з половиною разів, і це робиться для того, щоб мотивувати водіїв виїхати на виклики у райони з підвищеним попитом.
Олена Орлова, представниця українського сервісу виклику таксі: «Головна мета даного механізму в нашому випадку взагалі — збалансувати ринок сервісу виклику авто і зробити так, щоб максимальна кількість водіїв потрапила в ті райони, де найбільш підвищений попит».
Вплинути на це ціноутворення наразі не може ніхто, адже ринок таксі залишається неврегульованим.
Андрій Антонюк, директор ГО «Українська таксомоторна асоціація»: «Ринок на 99% є нелегальним. Люди працюють в основному не як суб’єкти підприємництва, не платять податки. І цій проблемі вже десятиріччя».
В уряді проблему визнають та оцінюють у конкретних цифрах.
Сергій Деркач, перший заступник міністра інфраструктури: «Державний бюджет недоотримує в рік близько 5 мільярдів гривень. Це виключно з тих податків, які мали б платитися в бюджет саме водіями таксі на сьогодні. Це немаленька сума, яку точно можна було витратити якраз на користь транспортної сфери, як мінімум».
Наразі Кабмін разом із народними депутатами готує реформу таксі. Насамперед планують з’ясувати точну кількість водіїв у країні через запровадження електронної реєстрації, яка дозволить отримати статус водія за добу. Пасажири матимуть доступ до інформації про керманича. Також передбачено податок для цифрових платформ служб таксі й доставок у розмірі 5,5% та їхню відповідальність за наявність у водіїв техогляду й страховки. відповідний законопроект вже проходить останні кола погодження і незабаром потрапить до парламенту.
Щодо диктування тарифів під час тривог: уряд не планує регулювати ціни зверху, посилаючись на європейський досвід, де це належить до компетенції місцевої влади. title: Украинский экс-футболист "Шахтера" дебютировал в немецкой Бундеслиге
content_c:
Защитник сборной Украины Ефим Конопля спустя полгода после ухода из "Шахтера" дебютировал за менхенгладбахскую "Боруссию" в немецкой Бундеслиге.
27-летний украинец вышел на замену на 70-й минуте выездного победного матча седьмого тура чемпионата Германии против "Штутгарта" (2:3).
Напомним, Конопля перешел в "Боруссию" Менхенгладбах в конце мая в статусе свободного агента, а начало сезона он пропустил из-за травмы.
Конопля родился в Донецке и является воспитанником академии "Шахтера". Он выступал за первую команду клуба с 2021 года после возвращения из аренды в "Десне".
Всего он провел 114 матчей во всех турнирах за "Шахтер", записав на свой счёт 7 голов и 15 результативных передач. Также в его активе 27 матчей и 2 гола за национальную сборную Украины.
Вместе с "Шахтером" футболист трижды становился чемпионом Украины, дважды выигрывал Кубок Украины и завоевывал Суперкубок Украины.
Ранее сообщалось о том, что украинский экс-футболист "Шахтера" оформил победный дубль в Саудовской Аравии.

title: В Києві до тепла підключені вже майже чверть закладів соцсфери – мер
content_c:
Мер Києва Віталій Кличко повідомив, що за перший тиждень опалювального сезону у Києві до тепла підключені вже майже кожен четвертий заклад соціальної сфери.
"Попри всі неправдиві закиди, що Київ нібито не готувався до опалювального сезону, ми першими в Україні розпочали його тиждень тому. Як зазвичай, спершу для закладів соціальної сфери. Окрім частини Дніпровського і Деснянського районів, де значних ушкоджень зазнали енергооб'єкти – там тривають відновлювальні роботи. За заявками керівників вже підключені до тепла майже чверть соцзакладів міста, зокрема, 49 медзакладів, 153 дитсадки та 23 школи", – повідомив Кличко у відеозверненні в п'ятницю.
За його словами, столичні лікарні повністю забезпечені резервними джерелами живлення. "Вони мають 480 генераторів. У 15 лікарнях уже є власні свердловини, ще 6 закладів завершують їх будівництво. 11 медзакладів – з автономним теплопостачанням від власних котелень. До кінця року можливість такого опалення матиме 21 столична лікарня", – повідомив Кличко.
Також забезпечені резервними джерелами енергії, засобами обігріву, запасами пального, води, медикаментів та продуктів харчування усі 25 міських установ соціального захисту. Для них придбано 134 генератори різних потужностей.
Як повідомлялося, Кличко заявив про старт опалювального сезону в Києві 16 жовтня. За його словами, опалюваний сезон спочатку, як зазвичай, "розпочнеться для закладів соціальної сфери, зокрема, в лікарнях, школах, садочках" за індивідуальними заявками їх керівників.

"Попри всі неправдиві закиди, що Київ нібито не готувався до опалювального сезону, ми першими в Україні розпочали його тиждень тому. Як зазвичай, спершу для закладів соціальної сфери. Окрім частини Дніпровського і Деснянського районів, де значних ушкоджень зазнали енергооб'єкти – там тривають відновлювальні роботи. За заявками керівників вже підключені до тепла майже чверть соцзакладів міста, зокрема, 49 медзакладів, 153 дитсадки та 23 школи", – повідомив Кличко у відеозверненні в п'ятницю.
За його словами, столичні лікарні повністю забезпечені резервними джерелами живлення. "Вони мають 480 генераторів. У 15 лікарнях уже є власні свердловини, ще 6 закладів завершують їх будівництво. 11 медзакладів – з автономним теплопостачанням від власних котелень. До кінця року можливість такого опалення матиме 21 столична лікарня", – повідомив Кличко.
Також забезпечені резервними джерелами енергії, засобами обігріву, запасами пального, води, медикаментів та продуктів харчування усі 25 міських установ соціального захисту. Для них придбано 134 генератори різних потужностей.
Як повідомлялося, Кличко заявив про старт опалювального сезону в Києві 16 жовтня. За його словами, опалюваний сезон спочатку, як зазвичай, "розпочнеться для закладів соціальної сфери, зокрема, в лікарнях, школах, садочках" за індивідуальними заявками їх керівників.

title: Hispanic voters helped bring Trump to power - in Texas, the tide may be turning
content_c:
Hispanic voters helped bring Trump to power - in Texas, the tide may be turning
- Published
It was just before dawn in the Rio Grande Valley in Texas and the congregation were arriving for the Friday service at the tiny La Lomita Catholic Chapel.
The whitewashed building, which has been here since the days of the American Civil War, rises from the surrounding scrub and sits about 200 yards from the Rio Grande river itself.
As cars pulled up to the chapel, the sound of Father Roy Snipes' barking dogs signalled his arrival. He has been the priest here for almost half a century - and is known locally as the Cowboy Priest.
"I'm not sure why I picked that up, but it's nice," he said of the nickname.
In truth, it is pretty obvious why. Snipes wears a Stetson in place of the more traditional priest's hat. And moments later, the chapel was filled by the sound of a Roy Rogers song - the singer and actor known as the King of the Cowboys.
During the first Trump administration, Snipes resisted plans to seize the chapel's land to build the US president's border wall. Eight years on, at the early Friday service, he focused his short sermon on the actions of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
"There's no good excuse to detain, incarcerate and deport poor, good folks who are our neighbours," Snipes told the congregation of about 30, mainly Hispanic worshippers.
Texas accounted for roughly one-third of all ICE arrests nationwide in July 2026 - a larger share than any other state - according to government figures obtained by the Deportation Data Project.
"They said we're gonna seek out, capture, detain and deport the worst of the worst," Snipes said in his sermon. "Well, we're here on the border and the cartel is the worst-of-the-worst. So we thought, well, that's a good thing.
"But it turned out, you can hear almost every day, some poor guy going to work and they stop him and detain him and start a big fight."
After the service, two members of the congregation stopped to chat. "We're educators, and we have a lot of students that are having to go back because their parents are getting deported," one said.
"The cruelty that we're seeing - I think that's turning the tide, at least I hope so," their friend added.
Turning the tide politically is what Democrats are hoping they can do in Texas in the midterm elections on 3 November. But that will not be easy.
This stretch of the Rio Grande was once one of the busiest crossing points on the US-Mexico border. Under former President Joe Biden, hundreds of thousands of migrants came through here, with more than two and a half million apprehensions recorded in a single year.
Trump promised to stop these illegal crossings during his 2024 election campaign, and in large parts he has delivered.
Border crossings are now at their lowest level in decades. And it was that promise which in part drove Trump's astonishingly high level of support in the state, taking around 55% of Hispanic votes in Texas alone - a record for a Republican presidential candidate.
Javier Villalobos is the Republican Mayor of McAllen, one of the biggest cities in the Rio Grande Valley. He expects Republicans will find it tough this time around, but credits the Trump administration with stemming the border problem.
"I remember I put out a video… thanking the administration for immediately securing the border. That was great," he said. "And I think generally most people are okay with the deportation of criminals, violent people, or people that really are not productive at all."
But if you start deporting people that are productive and law-abiding, that is where the problem is, he added.
Recent polls suggest much of Trump's support among Hispanic voters has ebbed away since 2024. Surveys taken since late summer indicate a majority of Texan Hispanic voters disapprove of the president. They also suggest Hispanic voters are favouring Democrats over Republicans by a significant margin.
"When I voted for President Trump, I voted for him because we saw an influx of immigration during the Biden administration," said Mario Guerrero, a young Mexican-American businessman who leads the South Texas Builders Association. It needed to be fixed, he said.
"We thought that we were in the right by voting for Trump, and that he was going to do what was best in order to fix the crisis on the border.
"And I think to myself, we were really not told the extreme that they were willing to go to make a point," he added, before referencing recent shootings involving ICE agents in US cities.
Guerrero is a reminder that, for many who live and work close to the US-Mexico border, security and immigration enforcement are two distinct issues.
A voter here may be supportive of securing the border and stopping illegal crossings, but oppose the actions of ICE and how the administration is enforcing its crackdown on undocumented migration.
Guerrero voted for Trump three times in a row - but is planning to vote Democrat in November, in part due to his unease with that crackdown.
"There's a man that I know that… last year, had 35 workers that were working for him every day," he said. "Right now, he just told me two days ago that he would be lucky if he would get four to six guys to show up to work."
Even though Guerrero plans to vote Democrat, he describes himself as neither Democrat nor Republican. And that, according to Mike Madrid, a leading Republican consultant and expert on Hispanic voters, is key to understanding the largest ethnic demographic voting group in the country.
"Latinos are more likely than any other racial or ethnic group to identify as independents rather than Republicans or Democrats," he said.
It was in part the belief that Hispanic voters were shifting permanently towards the Republican Party that led Trump to press states such as Texas to redraw their congressional maps early, before the once-a-decade census.
The strategy was intended to capitalise on what Republicans saw as a realignment in Hispanic voting behaviour, particularly in border districts that had been Democratic strongholds for more than a century.
Texas's 15th congressional district was among those that were redrawn, and has become one of the clearest tests of whether electoral maps can guarantee political outcomes.
The seat was redrawn after the 2020 census and was won by a Republican in 2022. It was redrawn again in 2025, creating a notional 18-point majority for Republicans in these midterms. Even so, current polling suggests a Democratic lead of five or six points.
Bobby Pulido is the Democratic candidate hoping to win the district. As a popular Tejano singer and winner of two Latin Grammys, he is already a household name in the Rio Grande Valley.
At an event just weeks before the vote, he delivered a stock political speech followed by a musical performance. "A lot of people are disillusioned with both parties," he told the BBC shortly before he took the stage. "And I hear them."
To win in this part of Texas, you need to be a conservative. Pulido has distanced himself from the national Democratic Party brand and focused deliberately and consistently on economic issues.
"This isn't New York, this isn't LA," he said. "When you lead with issues like social justice, climate change and other topics, that's not what people want to hear first. They want to hear about the economy."
That message is consistent with what many current polls are suggesting - the economy, and the cost of living specifically, rank top on the list of most voters' priorities.
At a local avocado festival, a fruit that is a staple among Hispanic communities in the valley, a couple, Dave Baldwin and Veronica Salazar, began discussing rising prices as soon as they were asked about the upcoming elections.
When asked who they blame for spiking costs, the answer was swift. "The president," they said.
"He is in control of our destiny with all that, and right now he's not doing a very good job," added Baldwin.
Among many Republican campaigners here, there is a feeling that they are are on the back foot just weeks before the vote.
Alexis Uscanga, a student volunteer tasked with knocking on doors and checking on likely Republican voters in the district, was realistic about what he is trying to achieve.
"The midterms are just purely a game of turnout," he said. "It's not trying so much to convince individuals to vote one way or the other, it's about trying to get our people mostly to show up."
Tano Tijerina, the Republican candidate in the neighbouring, Democratic-held 28th district, credited Trump with "breaking through barriers" but acknowledged the "national political headwinds are real".
The Hispanic shift towards President Trump in 2024 was one of the most striking political facts of the past decade. While this expanding demographic may not have much love for either party, in a two-party system voters are mostly forced to make a choice.
And if polling is correct - and there is no guarantee of that - even a modest swing back to Democrats in November could reshape races not just across this state but far beyond.
In Texas, it could even be enough to put a US Senate seat in play - and Democrats haven't won one of those in the state in more than 30 years.
Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here. Those outside the UK can sign up here.

title: ‘Comfort in a bowl’: porridge hotter than ever as fibremaxxers get their oats
content_c:
The clocks may be going back in the UK this weekend, but the biggest sign winter is coming is a steaming bowl of porridge on a breakfast table.
A staple for centuries, porridge is traditionally made with oats, water and a pinch of salt or sugar. However, the humble dish is now experiencing its own renaissance, with the latest iterations transforming it from drab to decadent. The trend is being driven by a growing fibre-centric movement as well as by nostalgia.
On social media, recipe creators are experimenting with everything from miso versions to sour cherry and pistachio butter toppings. At 26 Grains, a central London restaurant that specialises in porridge, this month’s offering includes a five-grain porridge topped with fig and red grape jam and a dollop of whipped cream. Over at Oatis in west London, toppings range from caramelised banana and tahini to mushrooms and pesto.
Alex Hely-Hutchinson, the founder of 26 Grains, describes porridge as “comfort in a bowl”. Part of its appeal, she says, is that it allows a “moment for pause in a busy world” – plus most people know how to make it.
It is a trend that is affecting home store cupboards. Searches for organic jumbo oats at Ocado are up 98% year on year while sales of White’s jumbo oats are up 56%.
Hedié Rhodes, the founder of the UK’s first dedicated cereals bakery, Husk & Honey in south London, describes the “personalisation aspect” of porridge as an instigator of the trend. Her brand, which began in 2015 specialising in granola, now also sells dedicated porridge blends. Bestsellers include cinnamon bark and cranberry and a spiced apple version.
“Porridge is a great carrier for a lot of nice things,” Rhodes says. “You can make a big pan of it and everyone in the family can still have a different style. Some might want it just with honey, others might want to add really fancy toppings.”
Alex Hayes, a co-founder of the food innovation studio Harris and Hayes, compares porridge to salads and smoothies. “It’s a great canvas for adding specific toppings that suit specific taste and nutritional needs,” she says, pointing to nut butters alongside more functional additions such as psyllium husk.
While protein mania isn’t slowing down, the online nutrition trend of “fibremaxxing” is encouraging more people to up their fibre intake. The NHS recommends adults should eat 30g of fibre a day, but according to the British Dietetic Association the average intake is only 18g. Oats are a source of the soluble fibre that is essential for gut health and can also help reduce cholesterol levels. So rather than eating protein-rich eggs for breakfast, many people are now reverting to a bowl of porridge.
On the menu at Café Cùil on the Isle of Skye you’ll find a “wee porridge” featuring pinhead oats that are soaked in oat milk overnight. Its founder, the chef and writer Clare Coghill, then finishes it with seasonal toppings. At the moment it’s a hazelnut praline brittle and poached pears.
Coghill, who recently tasted 86 bowls of porridge in her role on the judging panel of the world porridge-making championship that takes place in the Scottish Highlands each year, says “porridge purists” prefer to use coarser pinhead oats, also known as steel-cut oats, rather than rolled oats which are softer. “Pinhead were the original oats, so it’s a way of celebrating Scottish heritage,” she says.
Hely-Hutchinson opts for a mixture including jumbo oats and rolled oats for “creaminess”, along with rye, barley and malted wheat for added texture and “a slight fermented note”. Other recipes have ditched the oats altogether for rice, amaranth or quinoa.
To avoid a gloopy porridge, Coghill says stirring is key. “It’s all about slowly warming up the pot and constantly moving the spurtle [stirrer] around, which will create a really nice silky bowl of porridge.”
Hely-Hutchinson prefers hers “just right”, which for her is on the softer side. “Porridge is so nostalgic, I make it how my mum used to for me,” she says. “It all depends on the person. It’s like the same as how much Marmite someone puts on their toast or the amount of milk they put in their tea.”
Next, as porridge pivots from basic to bougie, is a move beyond the breakfast table. “People are increasingly busy and seem to be receptive to a more simple dish,” says Hely-Hutchinson, adding that customers get annoyed if porridge is not available on the menu past 3pm.
Hayes says we can expect to see more savoury options popping up on menus taking influence from Chinese congee, a traditional savoury rice pudding, and Indian kitchari, made with yellow split mung beans.
Rhodes points out that similar to how bakers experiment with wheat, people are now realising how much potential oats have. “It’s really interesting pushing the limits with oats. There are so many avenues to explore,” she says.
There is one downside to this new porridge passion, though: having to wash up the pan.
